articles.title: CNT-Mediated Integration of Pd and In2O3 Circumvents Activity–Stability Trade-Off in CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
articles.abstract: Metal promotion is a widely adopted strategy to enhance the activity of indium oxide (In2O3) catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, intimately contacted metal promoters on In2O3 often result in rapid catalyst deactivation, as excessive local H2 supply induces undesirable structural degradation of the In2O3 domain. Here, we address this limitation by implementing a carbon nanotube (CNT)-mediated hydrogen transport pathway, which spatially separates the H2 activation sites (Pd) from the CO2 hydrogenation sites (In2O3) at the catalyst preparation stage. Intriguingly, upon reductive activation, the initially separated components spontaneously evolve into a distinctive interfacial configuration. In this configuration, InOx migrates onto and partially covers the Pd nanoparticles, forming an InOx@Pd inverse interface. Unlike the directly constructed Pd–In2O3 interface, which suffers from over-reduction to metallic In0 accompanied by sintering and alloying with Pd, this CNT-derived interface preserves the In3+ oxidation state and serves as a non-destructive junction for hydrogen delivery. Combined with long-range hydrogen spillover across the CNT network, this architecture transforms a concentrated and destructive hydrogen flux into a regulated supply that reaches distal In2O3 domains without driving over-reduction. Consequently, the Pd/CNT + In2O3 system exhibits both improved catalytic activity and enhanced long-term stability (>230 h), whereas the conventional Pd/In2O3 catalyst deactivates continuously. These findings demonstrate that a controlled hydrogen delivery system between H2 activation sites and active sites on the oxide domain offers an effective way for developing active and durable catalysts involving reduction-sensitive oxide phases.

articles.title: Hydration Changes are Essential for Efficient Breakdown of Faropenem by the L1 Metallo-β-lactamase
articles.abstract: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. Benchmarking against B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d) shows that DFTB3 provides the best correlation between energy and structure for this system. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 participating in back-and-forth proton-transfer events and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. The calculated free energy barriers for the formation of both products are consistent with the experimentally determined catalytic constant, and the calculated greater stability of the imine with its crystallographic observation. These simulations provide dynamic insight into L1 catalysis, highlighting features that can be exploited for inhibitor design.

articles.title: Formamidinium-Solvent Intermediates Mediate Self-Seeding Crystallization for Efficient Inverted α-FAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.

articles.title: Improving the Calendar Life of Silicon Anodes with Inorganic Solid–Electrolyte Interphases
articles.abstract: Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.

articles.title: Membrane-Anchored Dual-Targeting Aptamer Engagers for Programmable T Cell Redirection in Solid and Hematological Cancers
articles.abstract: Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.

articles.title: Oncolytic Virus-like Nanoparticle Targets the Golgi Apparatus via Sphingomyelin
articles.abstract: The Golgi apparatus (GA) has emerged as a promising target for cancer therapy. Commonly, therapeutics are guided to the GA by recognizing specific receptors on the GA membrane. However, the low and heterogeneous expression of these receptors often results in suboptimal targeting efficiency. Here, we present an oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle for GA targeting by exploiting sphingomyelin, an abundant component of the GA membrane. This nanoparticle consisted of a polymeric nanocarrier complexed with a plasmid encoding the secreting peptide-deleted α-hemolysin (αHL), a pore-forming protein with high affinity for sphingomyelin. The nanoparticle could transfect cancer cells to induce intracellular expression of αHL, enabling GA targeting through binding to GA-associated sphingomyelin while bypassing the cell membrane. Consequently, the transfected cells exhibited GA structural disassembly and underwent a pyroptosis-like programmed cell death with immunogenic characteristics. Notably, αHL-rich microvesicles were subsequently secreted, effectively killing neighboring tumor cells. Intratumoral administration of this formulation significantly suppressed subcutaneous tumor growth and elicited robust antitumor immunity, preventing tumor rechallenge. Furthermore, by incorporating iRGD-modified polymers, we constructed a tumor-targeting oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle with neutral surface charge. Following intravenous administration, this iRGD-modified nanoparticle could efficiently suppress tumor growth without causing obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a robust strategy for GA-targeting via sphingomyelin recognition, providing a potential approach for GA-targeted anticancer therapeutics.

articles.title: pH-Programmed Poly(amino acid) Nanoparticles for Mucus-Penetrating and Bacteria-Targeted Eradication of Helicobacter pylori
articles.abstract: The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. Here, we report a pH-programmed poly(amino acid)-based nanoplatform for the precise eradication of H. pylori. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4–6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6–7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.

Multidimensional‐Encoded High‐Fidelity Spectrometers With a Floating‐Base Bipolar Junction
articles.abstract: Miniaturized computational spectrometers that combine spectrally tunable photodetectors with reconstruction algorithms offer a promising route toward compact, portable spectral sensing while maintaining performance comparable to traditional benchtop spectrometers. In single‐detector computational spectrometers, a reconfigurable photodetector serves as spectral‐encoding hardware, and the quality of its spectral response matrix critically determines peak‐wavelength accuracy, noise tolerance, and reconstruction fidelity. However, conventional encoding schemes based on electrically tunable single photodetectors often rely on one‐dimensional voltage sweeps, which can suffer from highly correlated response states and a practical trade‐off among electrical tunability, broadband coverage, and reconstruction robustness. Here, we address this trade‐off using a spectrally tunable floating‐base bipolar‐junction photodetector as a representative multidimensional encoder. By counter‐tuning the interfacial barrier matching between balanced and unbalanced configurations, a single detector combines excitonic‐resonance‐enhanced response, monotonic short‐wavelength absorption, and interlayer transport modulation of photoexcited carriers, thereby generating a richer and less correlated spectral response matrix. Multidimensional encoding of these complementary spectral response features enables more effective decoupling of encoded spectral datasets, even under sub‐nanoampere photocurrent operation where noise and calibration errors can critically degrade reconstruction fidelity. Our strategy provides a versatile pathway toward high‐fidelity, compact, and robust computational spectrometers for edge‐level spectral sensing and intelligent optoelectronic systems.

articles.title: Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysts with Trinuclear, Mixed‐Valence Iron Motifs on Electronically Aligned Carbon Dots
articles.abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a bottleneck for water electrolysis, remains limited by the adsorbate scaling relations and sluggish interfacial electron transfer (IET). We address these challenges by anchoring mixed‐valence Fe3+/Fe2+ motifs on aspartic‐acid–derived carbon dots (AspCDs). Spectroscopic analyses support trinuclear Fe3 sites, which offer redox flexibility and proximal active centers. The Fe3 site binds the substrate (OH−) and is electronically coupled to the AspCD scaffold. Together with the work function‐aligned scaffold for electron abstraction from OH−, these features establish effective inner‐sphere IET from OH−, through the active Fe3 center and the AspCDs host to the electrode. Simultaneously, the mixed valency buffers the charge build‐up during the successive proton‐coupled electron transfers. The catalyst drives fast and selective O2 generation and minimizes H2O2 formation, while sustaining at least ∼70 h of continuous operation with a gradual ∼90 mV total potential increase. Thus, the Fe3/AspCDs catalyst requires only 110 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm−2, shows particularly effective kinetics with a low Tafel slope of 41 mV dec−1, and has a turnover frequency of 2.1 s−1. The design integrates crucial physicochemical properties for highly efficient OER, and the principle can be generalized to other systems toward further advances in the field.

articles.title: Reflector‐Free, Highly Confined Love‐Like SAWs Enabled by a Phononic Metasurface for Real‐Time Monitoring of Cell Dynamics
articles.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices are widely used in sensing and biosensing but generally suffer from strong attenuation in liquid environments. Conventional approaches rely on reflectors to reduce these losses, yet these components remain difficult to optimize: limited device miniaturization and increased fabrication complexity. Here, we introduce an innovative design strategy that integrates a phononic metasurface with tailored electromechanical properties of the substrate to generate a type of shear‐horizontal (SH) surface resonance modes that exhibit strong lateral confinement and extremely low radiation into both the substrate bulk and the free surface, eliminating the need for reflectors. This approach enables highly tailorable surface acoustic resonances with distinctive enhanced dynamic strain‐energy confinement leading to significantly high‐quality factors, particularly in water‐loaded conditions. We show the fabrication and experimental validation of the proposed phononic metasurface‐based SAW resonator and showcase its biosensing capabilities through real‐time monitoring of cellular death.

articles.title: Uniformly Anchored Dibenzothiophene‐Armed Self‐Assembled Molecule Regulates Perovskite Lattice for Efficient and Stable Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The molecular aggregation of self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) and their weak anchoring to the perovskite layer result in interfacial non‑radiative recombination and perovskite degradation, significantly impeding improvements in the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, we design a novel π‐conjugated SAM, (4‐(3,6‐bis(dibenzo[b, d]thiophen‐2‐yl)‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (4PADBT), to simultaneously address these challenges. The introduction of two non‐coplanar dibenzothiophene (DBT) units onto the conventional 4PACZ backbone creates a large dihedral angle (∼70°), which effectively suppresses molecular aggregation and promotes the formation of uniform and well‐ordered SAM films. Furthermore, the DBT groups act as a pair of anchoring arms, forming strong coordination bonds between sulfur (S) atoms and Pb2+ ions at the buried interface. This uniform SAM layer and the strong interactions not only facilitate preferential (100) crystal orientation in the perovskite layer but also induce a lattice strain transition from tensile to compressive type, thereby effectively enhancing the structural stability and reducing defects. With these merits, the 4PADBT‐based device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.25%, significantly higher than the 23.82% of the control 4PACZ device. Moreover, this design improves both thermal and operational stabilities, highlighting 4PADBT as a promising interfacial material for high‐efficiency and stable PSCs.

articles.title: Artificial Regulatory T Cells Orchestrate Phase‐Spanning Regeneration in Refractory Tissue Injuries
articles.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) possess potent multiphasic reparative capacity; however, their application is limited by ethical and regulatory challenges associated with live cell therapies. Treg‐derived exosomes (TExo) exhibit low immunogenicity while enriching regenerative signaling relative to parental Tregs. Current exosome carriers place greater emphasis on sustained release than on factors affecting vesicle stability, such as nonspecific interactions and confinement effects. Inspired by the multivesicular body (MVB), we engineered artificial Tregs (ATregs) with an MVB‐like architecture that integrates vesicle protection with sustained release through a reconstructed storage microenvironment. This design enables phase‐aligned TExo release and extends functional activity by more than an order of magnitude compared with free TExo. ATregs sequentially coordinate the suppression of inflammation, enhancement of angiogenesis, and stimulation of skin appendage regeneration. In diabetic wounds and deep second‐degree burn models, which represent intrinsic repair dysfunction and severe structural tissue loss, ATregs markedly accelerate healing and outperform conventional strategies across murine and porcine models. These findings overcome the key limitations of exosome therapies and open a new avenue for next‐generation regenerative therapeutics.

articles.title: Biomaterial‐Based Controlled Release Systems for Spinal Cord Remyelination
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a complex secondary injury cascade characterized by oligodendrocyte (OL) death and axonal demyelination, leading to permanent neurological deficits. Despite the presence of endogenous oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), the inhibitory microenvironment—marked by inflammation, glial scarring, and biochemical barriers—prevents effective remyelination. Traditional pharmacological treatments are further hindered by the blood‐spinal cord barrier and rapid clearance of intrathecal injections. This review examines the evolution of controlled release systems engineered to modulate the oligodendroglial lineage. We analyze macro‐ and micro‐scale platforms, including scaffolds, which provide mechanical and topographical cues to direct the fate of OLs and OPCs. Furthermore, we discuss advanced nanoscale vectors, such as nanoparticles and exosomes, designed to deliver high‐value payloads—including small molecules and therapeutic oligonucleotides—directly to the lesion site while minimizing systemic toxicity. Finally, we address critical translational gaps to bridge the divide between preclinical innovation and clinical application in restoring neural connectivity.

articles.title: Remote‐Controlled Genetic Circuits: Light, Ultrasound, and Magnetic Fields for Programmable Gene Regulation
articles.abstract: Remote‐controlled genetic circuits use externally applied physical signals to regulate gene expression and cellular functions with spatial and temporal precision. Light, ultrasound, and magnetic fields provide complementary advantages in controllability, tissue accessibility, and biological compatibility, but their performance depends on both physical‐field propagation and efficient conversion of external energy into intracellular signals and predictable gene‐regulatory outputs. This review presents a unified framework of physical transduction, biological sensors, signal processors, and genetic effectors for comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems. Core genetic circuits are distinguished from delivery and auxiliary platforms that support cargo release, cellular uptake, or energy conversion without directly regulating genes. Representative systems are compared by circuit architecture, transduction mechanism, stimulus parameters, dynamic range, basal leakage, response kinetics, reversibility, in vivo actuation, delivery requirements, and safety. The evolution from inducible switches toward multi‐input logic, tunable regulation, genetic memory, and feedback control is discussed. An end‐to‐end codesign workflow and modality‐specific reporting framework are proposed to integrate physical inputs, transducers, genetic circuits, delivery strategies, and stimulation devices. Quantitative benchmarking and standardized safety evaluation are essential for advancing these systems toward predictable and clinically translatable therapeutic platforms.

articles.title: Silicate Biomaterials‐Stimulated Vascularized Callus Organoids for Bone Tissue Regeneration
articles.abstract: Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet‐based microfluidic platform for the high‐throughput generation of morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate‐engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube‐engineered composite hydrogel (2NT‐GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction‐related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical‐sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT‐GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.

Practical Considerations for Operando 7Li Nuclear Magnetic Resonance in Coin and Pouch Cells
articles.abstract: Operando nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insight into chemical changes in batteries during use but has largely been limited to custom plastic cells. Unfortunately, the metal casings that house commercial batteries distort and shield radiofrequency (RF) fields required for excitation and detection in NMR. Here, we use operando7Li NMR spectroscopy to study metal-encased batteries in both coin and pouch cell formats without modifying the cell or casing. We benchmark NMR spectra obtained from stainless-steel coin cells and aluminum-laminate pouch cells to plastic coin cells and show that casing composition, auxiliary hardware, and sample placement strongly influence observed shift, signal intensity, and line shape due to bulk magnetic susceptibility effects and RF attenuation upon interacting with cell parts. These effects are most severe in stainless-steel coin cells (and in particular 304-grade stainless steel) but can be mitigated through the use of Al spacers while retaining the stainless-steel caps and springs. In light of these considerations, we leverage operando7Li NMR to track lithium plating/stripping and monitor the accumulation of electrochemically inactive “dead” lithium (Li0) during galvanostatic cycling in coin and pouch cells. In pouch cells, the lean electrolyte volume allows us to resolve changes in the 7Li electrolyte signal during formation that are consistent with electrolyte redistribution and wetting. Taken together, these results demonstrate how to alter cell susceptibility to improve NMR signals during operando measurements in commercially relevant form factors while also establishing the cell design constraints that limit quantitative interpretation.

articles.title: Unraveling the Mystery of Near-Infrared Emission in an Antimony Halide Dimer Driven by the Jahn–Teller Effect
articles.abstract: Most zero-dimensional hybrid metal halides enable emission in the first near-infrared (NIR-I) region (650–950 nm), and the shorter wavelengths result in poor photon penetration depth. Here, we report the observation of an NIR-II emission signal (band gap = 1.13 eV) from a (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 single crystal at room temperature. Although a variety of mechanisms are involved in the explanation of such a broad band with a large Stokes shift, the exploration of the structural origin of the NIR optical activity remains challenging due to misconceptions about excitons and experimental limitations. A strategy that spatially confines 5s2 ions within edge-shared [Sb2Cl8]2– units with controlled lattice distortion is proposed to cause a Jahn–Teller effect (JTE) during the interconfiguration transition (3P1 → 1S0). A family of hybrid metal halides doped with Bi3+,In3+ or Bi3+/In3+ demonstrates that the fine interplay between the Jahn–Teller effect and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) takes into full consideration orbital degeneracy and electron flipping, thus boosting the photoluminescence quantum yield to 12%. TD-DFT calculations visualize the symmetry of the two lattices within a dimeric structure varying with specific modes, and the rational assignment of the energy gap (ground state: 3.69 eV; excited state: 1.22 eV) between 1S0 and 3P1 is highly consistent with the experimental findings (λex = 330 nm; λem = 1100 nm). Leveraging the (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 sample, electroluminescence pumped by a UV-LED chip yields a highly efficient NIR-II emission, and the phosphor displays diverse functions in night vision and anticounterfeiting.

Shrubs benefit from being functionally more conservative and distinct from neighbour trees
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Multi‐strata forests can enhance ecosystem functioning, with interactions between overstorey trees and understorey shrubs playing a pivotal role. However, how the structure and composition of neighbouring trees, together with shrub traits, influence shrub growth remains poorly understood. In a large‐scale subtropical biodiversity experiment manipulating tree and shrub species richness, we inventoried 4411 shrubs and their surrounding trees after 11 years of interactions. We found that individual shrub biomass declined with increasing neighbour tree species richness, basal area and functional diversity, but exhibited a U‐shaped trend with the proportion of ectomycorrhizal‐associated neighbour tree individuals. Shrubs with more conservative resource‐use strategies attained higher biomass, particularly when surrounded by trees with low functional diversity and a high proportion of ectomycorrhizal associations. Biomass was also greater when shrubs were more resource‐conservative and functionally distinct from the neighbouring trees. Our findings highlight how shrub functional traits, combined with tree diversity, competition and functional traits, shape tree–shrub interactions, with shrubs benefiting more from resource‐conservative and functionally distinct traits relative to their neighbouring trees. articles.title: Why don't all birds lay early? Causes and consequences of breeding timing for a long‐lived migratory seabird
articles.abstract: Why don't all birds lay early? Our 16‐year study of Manx shearwater behaviour shows that selection on breeding timing fluctuates among years. We also find that lay dates are influenced by persistent individual differences, variation in non‐breeding duration, and pair synchrony, potentially constraining breeding phenological advancement under ongoing climate change. Abstract The relationship between earlier laying and higher breeding success is well‐established in avian species. However, a wide distribution of breeding timings is often maintained within a population, and the causes and consequences of this variation require further exploration, particularly as many avian species advance breeding phenology in response to climate change. Using a 16‐year dataset combining colony observations and biologging of Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus), we show that earlier laying does not always result in higher breeding success, with later laying becoming less costly in recent years. We additionally report a slight advancement in breeding timing within breeding pairs, despite finding no temporal trends in spring bloom onset. Nonetheless, birds adjusted lay date in response to interannual variation in phytoplankton bloom timing, and years with stronger Celtic Sea blooms exhibited stronger selection for early breeding. Breeding timing was also influenced by repeatable individual differences in migratory behaviour, with birds undertaking generally earlier, shorter migrations to less southerly destinations laying earlier across years. However, lay date was not determined solely by individual behaviour. In this long‐lived species with stable pair bonds, the arrival date of the second‐returning bird constrained advancement in laying. This study suggests that variation in breeding timing is maintained through the combined effects of fluctuating selection, persistent individual differences, variation in non‐breeding duration and pair‐level processes. articles.title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

articles.title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

articles.title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

articles.title: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. .The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer. Computational pathway analysis identified the possibility of an alternative, noncovalent route mediated by Arg283 and a heme propionate with possible electronic coupling comparable to that of the native tryptophan pathway. Consistent with this prediction, only simultaneous disruption of both the tryptophan and propionate-mediated pathways abolished bis-FeIV formation entirely. Moreover, only mutants capable of forming bis-FeIV retained the ability to turnover substrate, directly establishing this high-valent state as the catalytic intermediate responsible for substrate modification. These results demonstrate that an intervening tryptophan is not required for fast interheme electron transfer, and instead reveal an additional, noncovalent pathway that may be a general feature of diheme peroxidases.

articles.title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

articles.title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and >85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

articles.title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for preparing propene and succinic acid from CO2 hydrogenation.

articles.title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

articles.title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Experimental assignment of aromaticity in all-metal systems remains challenging, particularly for heavy-element clusters, where local magnetic effects can obscure signatures of circular electron delocalization. Here, we investigate a supramolecularly stabilized, formally tetracationic [Bi4]4+ ring by combining structurally meaningful reference compounds, solid- and solution-state NMR spectroscopy, SQUID magnetometry, and exact two-component relativistic calculations. Comparison with an isostructural [Li4Br]3+-encapsulated analogue and a binuclear Bi(III) reference compound disentangles global ring-current effects from local heavy-atom deshielding and ligand-specific conformational effects. On this basis, the unusually downfield-shifted 1H and 13C NMR signals observed for the Bi4-containing species provide direct spectroscopic evidence for magnetically induced ring currents in the [Bi4]4+ core. By contrast, bulk magnetic measurements do not reveal significant diamagnetic exaltation, indicating that this quantity is not a resolved descriptor of aromaticity in these systems. Stoichiometric studies further identify chemically competent intermediates that provide mechanistic snapshots of [Bi4]4+ ring formation. Complementary calculations support the assignment of a magnetically responsive, σ-delocalized [Bi4]4+ core, reproduce a rare spectroscopically observed puckering motion of the rhomboidal [Bi4]4+, and underscore the critical role of spin–orbit coupling on electronic structure and dynamics. Overall, this work moves the discussion of aromaticity from predominantly computational assignment toward experimentally benchmarked analysis in the heavy-element and all-metal regime.

articles.title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to >20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.

articles.title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

articles.title: Solvent-Coordination-Controlled Separation of Critical Metals from Spent Li-ion Batteries with Full Solvent Recovery
Synergistic local electronic regulation and interfacial reconstruction toward high-voltage and long-life manganese-based Prussian blue cathodes for potassium-ion batteries
Competing Magnetic Configurations Enable Low-Field Magnetoresistance Switching in Cr3Te4
articles.abstract: Large magnetoresistance typically emerges from transitions between distinct electronic phases or magnetic configurations, yet controllable switching between competing magnetic configurations within a single metallic material remains challenging. Here we investigate magnetotransport in Cr3Te4 and demonstrate a magnetic-field-switchable resistance modulation of up to −37.6%, enabled by the near degeneracy between antiparallel and parallel magnetic configurations. Remarkably, a magnetic field of ∼0.25 T suffices to induce switching between these competing magnetic configurations, accompanied by a reconstruction in electronic transport supported by Boltzmann transport calculations. Substituting 5% of Cr with Co suppresses the switching behavior, consistent with a suppression of the competition between the nearly degenerate magnetic configurations, while the magnetoresistance evolves into a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, suggesting a possible Weyl-band-related contribution associated with a Co-induced upward shift of the Fermi level. Our results establish competing magnetic configurations as an effective route toward large magnetoresistance in structurally simple metallic systems.

articles.title: Continuously Tunable Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance of Anisotropic Gold Nanopolyhedrons for Multiplexed Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Imaging
articles.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for multiplex bioimaging owing to its excellent photostability and ultranarrow spectral bandwidth. However, achieving synergistic enhancement of excitation and Raman scattering fields remains challenging. Herein, the relationship between geometry and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) was investigated by continuously tuning the aspect ratio (AR) of anisotropic Au nanopolyhedrons (Au NPHs). Central-body modulation while preserving sharp terminal tips enables continuous LSPR tuning while retaining tip-associated electromagnetic enhancement. The SERS behavior was further analyzed by considering the spectral matching between the LSPR and the excitation/scattering wavelengths. For different excitation wavelengths, the optimal SERS response can be achieved by selecting Au NPHs whose LSPR band best matches with the excitation and Raman scattering wavelengths. These results demonstrate that Raman enhancement is governed by spectral matching rather than a fixed optimal geometry. The optimized Au NPHs enabled the use of dual SERS probes for proof-of-concept multiplex biomarker imaging.

articles.title: Experimental Signature of Transient Symmetry Breaking in a Cavity Dirty-Limit Superconductor
articles.abstract: Transient states of matter far from equilibrium may exhibit physical properties beyond those allowed by the equilibrium-state crystalline symmetries. We explore ultrafast and direct electronic excitations of transient states in a dirty-limit superconductor with time-resolved terahertz-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy. By embedding the superconductor into a designed microcavity structure of metallic split-ring resonators, we can sensitively probe the pump field-induced transient variations of the superconducting states around the cavity’s resonant frequency. Our results show that the strong terahertz field can transiently modify the symmetries of the electronic subsystems via the injection of a picosecond supercurrent, leading to high-order nonlinear dynamical responses that are not compatible with the equilibrium-state symmetries, which is evidence for transient symmetry breaking on the picosecond time scale.

articles.title: Probing Valence Electron Distributions at Subatomic Resolution in a Charge Density Wave Material
articles.abstract: Probing the internal electronic structure of complex materials with atomic spatial resolution has remained an outstanding challenge in condensed-matter science. A promising approach is convergent-beam electron diffraction (CBED) in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Here, we apply 4D-STEM CBED to the charge-density-wave (CDW) material 1T-TaS2. We demonstrate a qualitative breakdown of the conventional independent atom model (IAM) in reproducing the experimental CBED patterns. A robust low-angle intensity maximum is systematically absent in IAM-based simulations but is consistently reproduced in simulations that use electrostatic potentials derived from density functional theory. A comparison of CBED patterns with projected charge densities reveals a remarkable correspondence between the local real-space valence charge distribution and diffracted intensities, reflecting site-dependent charge density variations within the CDW structure. These results establish atomic-resolution CBED as an experimental probe of valence electron contributions to the scattering potential and open a route to resolving complex electronic ordering phenomena.

articles.title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation
CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
articles.abstract: Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

articles.title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
articles.abstract: Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

articles.title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
articles.abstract: Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H2S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii. Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H2S-production with inflammatory diseases. Here, by compiling and analyzing a database of 2,658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases, the authors uncovered species-specific traits linked to impaired immune tolerance, providing a key resource for understanding their role in human disease.

articles.title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
articles.abstract: Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μ m thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

articles.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
articles.abstract: The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

articles.title: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
articles.abstract: Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1 , co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.

articles.title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
articles.abstract: Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

articles.title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
articles.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HOx radicals, promoting surface ozone (O3) and secondary fine particle (PM2.5) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005–2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (−47.4% in 2013–2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005–2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NOx and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NOx control in summer and co-reduction of NOx, PM2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O3 and PM2.5 joint mitigation. Deep learning reveals a sharp decline of HONO in China, modest drops in EU and US but an increase in India. HONO changes drive O3 and PM2.5 variations, outweighing traditional NOx and VOC control, calling for HONO-targeted air quality management.

articles.title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming
Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
articles.abstract: Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact. Mentalising is essential for social interaction and is thought to rely on the medial prefrontal cortex. Here, the authors show that damage to the medial prefrontal cortex leaves mentalising intact but alters how quickly people make social decisions.

articles.title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging
articles.abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing. This work presents a super-resolution quantum biosensing approach by integrating nitrogen vacancy (NV) center-based quantum nanodiamond sensors with structured illumination microscopy, which achieves super-resolution multi-physical imaging within live cells.

articles.title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
articles.abstract: Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

articles.title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
articles.abstract: Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd -Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in At AMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd -Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

articles.title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
articles.abstract: In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

Synthesis, mechanical properties and hardness-toughness synergy of micro/nanostructured superhard materials
[Comment] 21st century global threats to health are not what you think
articles.abstract: The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health's report by Christopher J L Murray and colleagues uses forecasts based on expected cumulative amenable disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) to quantify and compare threats from 2025 to 2100.1 The Commission's intent is to equip governments with the tools to make smart long-term decisions that reduce risk based on “systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning” as opposed to “short-termism and localism”.

articles.title: [Lecture] 50 years of Ebola research and response
articles.abstract: These are two lectures that form the Virchow Prize Lecture given by the authors in October, 2026. The first lecture was given by Peter Piot. The second lecture was given by Jean-Jacques Muyembe-Tamfum.

articles.title: [Perspectives] John Wong: making an impact on population health at scale
articles.abstract: “I’m concerned that the narrative now around ageing populations is one of doom and gloom. But long-lived populations are not the problem. The problem is that we haven’t allowed people to get to an older age healthy”, says John Wong, Executive Director of the Centre for Population Health at the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Executive Director of The Yong Pung How and Yong Wei-Woo Centre at the National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore. “Two-thirds of the world is now below the fertility replacement rate, and unless we keep our populations healthy throughout their whole lifespan, we’ll have this major challenge of more and more unwell older people”, continued Wong, who is also Isabel Chan Professor in Medical Sciences in the Division of Haematology-Oncology at the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, NUS, and Emeritus Consultant in the Department of Haematology-Oncology, National University Cancer Institute, NUHS, Singapore.

articles.title: [Review] Addressing threats to future global health—what is the right timeframe?
articles.abstract: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. Insofar as we protect the planet or invest in fruitful research on pandemic countermeasures, we promote future wellbeing and health, sometimes at the present generation's expense. As we warm the planet, accelerate antibiotic resistance, or consume finite natural resources, we might serve present-day wellbeing or health at the expense of future generations. To decide which such trade-offs are legitimate or advisable, we need to know how to balance the health interests of future generations against each other and against our own.

articles.title: [The Lancet Commissions] The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health
articles.abstract: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century. We argue that recent global shocks (including COVID-19, Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, major geopolitical conflict, accelerating climate impacts, rapid shifts in development assistance, and the emergence of powerful artificial intelligence [AI] systems) show how quickly assumptions about stability can be overturned—and why governments and multilateral institutions must counter short-termism and localism with systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning.

articles.title: A Bayesian approach to volumetric analysis in rare neurodegenerative disorders
articles.abstract: Identifying regional brain atrophy is critical for understanding neurodegenerative disorders. Traditionally, group comparisons rely on frequentist statistics, utilising $p$-values and point estimates that offer limited characterization of uncertainty. Bayesian methods provide an alternative by estimating effect sizes and credible intervals while incorporating prior knowledge and uncertainty. This study evaluated the feasibility of Bayesian hierarchical modelling to assess regional brain atrophy in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) and Corticobasal Syndrome (CBS) compared to healthy controls. Participants meeting diagnostic criteria for CBS or PSP, together with healthy controls, were recruited from the Cambridge Centre for Parkinson-plus. Grey matter volume, cortical thickness, and subcortical volumes were derived using FreeSurfer for 210 cortical and 36 subcortical regions defined by the Human Brainnetome Atlas. Participants with PSP were classified into Richardson syndrome (PSP-RS), corticobasal syndrome variant (PSP-CBS), frontal variant (PSP-F), and other presentations (PSP-Other). Bayesian hierarchical ANOVA models with appropriate priors were used to estimate group differences. Regions of practical equivalence (ROPE) were calculated to assess evidence of meaningful group effects. A total of 428 people were included (113 PSP-RS, 30 PSP-CBS, 23 PSP-Other, 19 PSP-F, 81 CBS, and 162 healthy controls). For grey matter volume, there was evidence of whole brain volume loss compared to controls for all disease groups except PSP-Other, which showed evidence of no difference. For cortical thickness, there was evidence of global cortical thinning in CBS compared to controls, but for no other group. For subcortical volume all groups showed evidence of volume loss compared to controls. Patterns of regional atrophy were identified in keeping with previous literature, with the largest effect observed in the left pre-motor thalamus (30\% reduction in CBS). There was greater loss of subcortical volume in PSP-RS compared to other PSP subgroups.
