Bayesian hierarchical modelling provides a feasible framework for quantifying regional brain atrophy, with interpretable effect size estimates and uncertainty measures. This approach complements conventional statistical methods, particularly in the assessment of rare neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Medical Research Council, https://ror.org/03x94j517, G1100464 Cambridge National Institute for Health Research Biomedical Research Centre, NIHR203312

articles.title: A Computational Model Captures Orexin-Dependent Modulation of Memory Consolidation.
articles.abstract: Hippocampal sharp-wave ripple (SWR) events occur during post-experience rest and sleep and play a significant role in memory consolidation. Recent ex vivo studies have found orexin-driven neuromodulatory effects on SWR parameters and proposed that they can influence memory consolidation. Additionally, behavioral studies demonstrate contradictory results regarding orexinergic effects on memory acquisition depending on task structure and intervention time. This inconsistency, along with the diffuse spread of orexin receptors (OXR) in the CA1 and CA3 hippocampus, challenges theoretical interpretation of orexinergic effects on memory. To reconcile this problem, we propose a rate-based model linking orexinergic tone-dependent SWR statistics to memory performance. The model combines an encoding module whose gain scales with the global orexinergic tone with a consolidation module driven by OX2R-specific replay dynamics. The model is based on a plasticity rule that considers SWR events as the unit of induction. Therefore, weight change requires sufficient replay content and depolarizing drive. We observed that, depending on the task structure, encoding-dominant learning benefits discrimination as the orexin drive increases. Consolidation-dominant learning shows a non-monotonic relationship with an internal optimum level of orexinergic tone. This interaction highlights that stronger truncation at higher receptor engagement shortens memory replay and reduces the efficacy of the consolidation process. The model predicts that the optimal regime depends on task complexity reflected in sequence length. Together, these results demonstrate how task demands determine whether increased orexinergic drive enhances or impairs effective consolidation and SWR-dependent replay in the hippocampus. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: A domesticated prophage enzyme links bacterial metabolism, episymbiosis and phage fitness
articles.abstract: Prophages are increasingly recognized as drivers of bacterial adaptation, yet how domesticated prophage genes shape microbial symbiosis remains poorly understood. Here, we identify GDPDXhp1, a glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase encoded by prophage Xhp1 of Schaalia odontolytica XH001, as a metabolic regulator linking bacterial physiology, episymbiosis and phage fitness. Association with the epibiotic bacterium Nanosynbacter lyticus TM7x strongly induced gdpdXhp1 expression and triggered GDPDXhp1-dependent lipid droplet accumulation in XH001. GDPDXhp1 orchestrated glycerophospholipid remodeling, membrane biophysical properties, respiration and cell-surface glycan composition in XH001, thereby promoting TM7x episymbiosis. Remarkably, GDPDXhp1 was also required for productive Xhp1 infection by remodeling susceptible bacterial host envelope structures to facilitate phage-host interactions. Together, our findings reveal a domesticated prophage enzyme that contributes to bacterial metabolism, interspecies symbiosis and viral reproduction, highlighting prophage as an overlooked source of metabolic innovation in microbial symbiosis. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research, 1R01DE023810, R01DE030943, 1R01DE031274 K99/R00, DE033794

articles.title: A mast cell receptor is associated with fibrosis and itch in systemic sclerosis
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by symmetric fibrosis of the skin and multiple internal organs. The mechanisms that trigger early fibrotic changes remain unclear. Mast cells are known to infiltrate human SSc lesional skin in early disease stages, yet the role of mast cells in initiating fibrosis and pruritus in SSc remains debated, in part due to unclear pathways of mast cell activation. Here, we show that mast cells, via the receptor Mrgprb2, contribute to fibrosis in the bleomycin (BLM)-induced skin fibrosis mouse model. Mast cells accumulate in the skin of BLM-treated wild-type (WT) but not Mrgprb2-knockout (Mrgprb2-/-) mice. Mrgprb2-/- mice show attenuated disease severity, with reduced collagen deposition and lower expression of matrix metalloproteinases and inflammatory markers associated with fibrosis. BLM treatment also increases pruritus in WT mice in the early stages of the model; an effect reduced in Mrgprb2-/- mice. This is the first report of itch in this model of skin fibrosis, further linking it to clinical SSc, where pruritus is an early and prevalent symptom affecting nearly half of patients. In a parallel human cohort, lesional SSc skin harbors significantly more mast cells than paired non-lesional skin from the same patients, demonstrating that mast cell accumulation is specific to affected tissue. Lesional mast cell counts also track with skin disease severity, correlating with modified Rodnan skin score and patient-reported skin tightness. Together, these findings implicate Mrgprb2-mediated mast cell activity in both fibrosis and pruritus in SSc, highlighting mast cells as a candidate therapeutic target in this understudied disease process. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institutes of Health, https://ror.org/01cwqze88, R37NS054791

articles.title: A modular DNA toolkit for single-molecule biophysics
articles.abstract: Long, customizable DNA molecules are an essential tool for in vitro single-molecule biophysics. Most studies still rely on the λ-phage genome, which has a fixed sequence, a non-uniform GC distribution, and limited options for modification. To overcome these limitations, we developed a modular DNA (ModDNA) toolkit that integrates in silico sequence design with cloning, to create long (up to 100 kb) DNA molecules with entirely user-defined sequences. We used a computational workflow with curated databases to design a motif-depleted sequence backbone, into which any desired sequence can be inserted at any position. Golden Gate assembly then builds these sequences into constructs, which we extend iteratively in defined increments up to 100 kb. We show precise placement of local features, e.g. a fluorophore, a bound protein, and a DNA-origami structure, and illustrate the construct's utility in single-molecule visualization assays, including DNA loop extrusion by human condensin I. ModDNA offers a scalable, sequence-programmable alternative to λ-DNA and other restrictive substrates. More broadly, the motif-aware feature-free design connects single-molecule biophysics to emerging efforts in machine-guided regulatory-sequence design and synthetic-genome engineering, where controlled programmable sequence context is increasingly essential. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: A niche-specific role for ArlRS enables Staphylococcus aureus growth within Kupffer cells
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections cause severe morbidity and mortality despite antibiotic therapy. We previously identified Kupffer cells (KCs) as the primary hepatic macrophages that rapidly clear circulating S. aureus, yet a subset of bacteria survives intracellularly and seeds systemic infection. Here, using spinning-disk intravital and super-resolution microscopy, we show that bacterial two-component system (TCS) signaling is required for intracellular replication within KCs in vivo. A global mutant lacking all non-essential TCSs failed to form intracellular microcolonies, and targeted analysis identified the ArlRS system as specifically required for KC replication. ΔarlRS bacteria remained as single non-replicating organisms within KCs, exhibited reduced dissemination and kidney abscess formation, and showed attenuated virulence with improved host survival. Complementation with arlRS restored the wildtype phenotype. Notably, the intracellular replication defect was not observed in primary or cultured macrophages, indicating that ArlRS-dependent replication is highly niche-specific and not reproduced by conventional in vitro models. Furthermore, restricting the KC reservoir with vancomycin treatment after infection further reduced renal infection by ΔarlRS bacteria. These findings identify ArlRS as a critical regulator of intracellular replication within KCs and establish the KC intracellular reservoir as a key driver of S. aureus pathogenesis and a potential therapeutic target during bloodstream infection. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: A semi-automated tool for improving Assessments and Lab Tests data annotation in ImmPort
articles.abstract: Public data sharing in immunological and clinical research is essential for transparency, reproducibility, and secondary analysis. However, many datasets in repositories such as ImmPort lack sufficient structured data to enable reuse. ImmPort's Assessments and Lab Tests templates — which capture critical clinical information — are often incomplete or omitted due to their complexity and the manual effort required. To address this challenge, an application with a graphical user interface requiring no programming was developed to facilitate population of these templates. The tool streamlines the submission process by reducing time and complexity for data contributors while ensuring template formatting. It integrates ImmPort files, study-specific data files, and a curated data dictionary to automate the mapping of study variables to the required fields within each template. The tool was evaluated on seven ImmPort studies with diverse designs. It successfully generated submission-ready templates that passed ImmPort's internal validation and will be incorporated into the repository. By improving the feasibility and completeness of templates, this approach enhances the quality, findability, and reusability of data within ImmPort. ### Competing Interest Statement M.D.S., P.P., H.S., and P.D. are current or former contributors to the ImmPort project. M.D.S. and P.P. are employees of ICF International, Inc., a contractor supporting ImmPort. H.S. was formerly employed by ICF, and P.D. was formerly employed by Peraton, Inc., another contractor supporting ImmPort, during portions of this work. The remaining authors declare no competing interests. National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), R03AI185587, UH2AI145837 National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), P30AR070549

articles.title: AMMPER-2: A spatially explicit agent-based model of microbial radiobiology with redox dye simulation
articles.abstract: To reduce health risks for human space exploration, it is important to model the effects of deep-space radiation on biological systems. The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a common model organism in space radiobiology, but little is known about how radiation damage to individual cells translates into the population-level effects that experiments measure. The Agent-Based Model for Microbial Populations Exposed to Radiation (AMMPER) is a spatially explicit agent-based model that simulates the effects of ionizing radiation on S. cerevisiae cells and produces population-level results. Its goal is to improve experiment design and data interpretation. AMMPER-1 demonstrated that agent-based simulations can qualitatively reproduce the effects of proton radiation on the growth rate of wild-type and DNA-repair mutant yeast. Here, we present AMMPER-2, which addresses limitations of the first model and expands its capabilities. AMMPER-2 incorporates the dynamics of the redox dye alamarBlue, a data type commonly generated in spaceflight microbiology experiments, and models the fate of reactive oxygen species in more detail. It also adds an improved graphical interface and runs faster. AMMPER-2 remains easy to execute in Python on a standard personal laptop, providing space biologists a tool to explore experimental conditions, generate hypotheses, and interpret data from microbial space radiation experiments. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Gulf Coast Consortia on the NLM Training Program in Biomedical Informatics and Data Science, T15 LM007093 National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program, 2024370642

articles.title: ASC specks and α-synuclein amplify microglial NLRP3 inflammasome activation and co-localize with Lewy body pathology
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of several chronic neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and other synucleinopathies, and is closely associated with microglial activation. The inflammasome adaptor protein apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain (ASC) undergoes oligomerization upon inflammasome activation, resulting in the formation of ASC specks. These structures are recognized by microglia as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), thereby promoting inflammatory signaling. Recent studies have demonstrated that extracellular ASC specks associate with amyloid-β (Aβ), and that uptake of ASC-Aβ composites by microglia amplifies pro-inflammatory responses. Although ASC specks have also been shown to potentiate α-synuclein (αSyn) preformed fibril-induced pathology, their interaction with monomeric αSyn and their effects on inflammasome activation remain poorly understood. Here, we co-stimulated murine SIM-A9 microglia with ASC-αSyn assemblies and evaluated their effects on NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Electron microscopy revealed a close association between ASC fibrils and αSyn monomers. Exposure of microglia to ASC-αSyn enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, as evidenced by increased ASC speck formation, caspase-1 activation, and secretion of IL-1β and IL-18, when compared to ASC or αSyn alone. In addition, immunohistochemical analyses of post mortem brain tissue from patients with dementia with Lewy bodies demonstrated ASC expression in regions exhibiting αSyn pathology and showed ASC co-localization with αSyn within Lewy bodies. Collectively, these findings identify ASC-αSyn assemblies as potent amplifiers of NLRP3 inflammasome signaling and suggest a mechanism through which they may contribute to sustained neuroinflammation in synucleinopathies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Research Council Canada, New Beginning Initiative, INBR4-000806

articles.title: Complete ammonia-oxidizing Nitrospira and ammonia-oxidizing archaea as biological supplements for freshwater aquaria
articles.abstract: Biological filtration in newly established aquaria depends on the establishment of nitrifying microorganisms that prevent accumulation of toxic ammonia and nitrite. Many aquarists use commercial nitrifying supplements to accelerate biofilter establishment and reduce ammonia and nitrite accumulation. However, the microbial composition and in situ efficacy of these products remain poorly characterized. We evaluated the ability of enrichment cultures containing comammox Nitrospira (CX) and the ammonia-oxidizing archaeon Ca. Nitrosotenuis aquarius (AQ) to serve as aquarium nitrifying supplements, tested alongside a conventional supplement (CS) containing ammonia-oxidizing bacteria. Inoculation of new aquaria containing zebrafish (Danio rerio) with nitrifying supplements resulted in distinct nitrifier profiles within biofilters of each treatment group corresponding with significant reductions in peak ammonia and nitrite concentrations, which were most evident when applied at the maximum tested supplement dose. Treating aquaria with CX, AQ, or CS maintained ammonia and nitrite at low concentrations, and CX effectively prevented ammonia and nitrite accumulation through all stages of aquarium operation and biofilter establishment. After removing all fish from the aquaria, ammonia "spike-in" experiments demonstrated biofilters treated with CX and AQ conferred long-term protection against nitrite accumulation following acute ammonia loading events. Whereas 16S rRNA gene sequences associated with CS were rarely detected within biofilter profiles, those associated with CX and AQ established early and persisted temporally. Overall, results demonstrate how nitrifiers might be differentially adapted to home aquarium conditions and the potential of AOA and comammox Nitrospira to improve biofilter establishment and maintaining safe water quality in newly established freshwater aquaria.

articles.title: Exchange of metabolic pathway intermediates as the origin for metabolite cross-feeding interactions in E. coli auxotrophic co-cultures
articles.abstract: A large fraction of microbes in natural environments are auxotrophs that rely on metabolite exchange for growth. The Black Queen hypothesis and related frameworks explain gene loss and reliance on shared metabolites. Yet it is not fully understood how metabolite cross-feeding emerges and gives rise to experimentally observable community performance. Here, we propose that exchange of biosynthetic pathway intermediates provides a mechanistic route for the emergence of metabolite cross-feeding. Building on prior work demonstrating intermediate exchange in E. coli auxotrophs, we investigated co-cultures between a methionine auxotroph (ΔmetA) and a panel of histidine auxotrophs. Among these, only ΔhisD exhibited efficient co-culture growth with ΔmetA, suggesting a unique role for the final step of histidine biosynthesis, which converts histidinol to histidine. We found that ΔmetA-ΔhisD co-cultures accumulated high levels of extracellular histidinol (>200 μM), suggesting a mechanism for metabolite exchange. Spent media from these co-cultures supported growth of all histidine auxotrophs except ΔhisD, confirming that histidinol, rather than histidine, was the dominant exchanged metabolite. Furthermore, we observed that ΔmetA efficiently converted histidinol to histidine only under methionine-limited conditions, suggesting that nutrient limitation promoted overflow of converted histidine to the extracellular environment. To quantitatively assess whether histidinol exchange could account for the observed co-culture behavior, we constructed a mechanistic model that links extracellular histidinol dynamics to co-culture growth through independently measured conversion capacity of the ΔmetA strain. Rather than fitting growth empirically, we used experimentally derived parameters to predict co-culture growth from the measured histidinol-to-histidine conversion flux. The model accurately recapitulated the timing and magnitude of growth and population dynamics, supporting the idea that accumulation of histidinol enabled the conversion-driven supply of histidine that sustained ΔhisD, while coupling growth between the two strains. Taken together, these results suggest that metabolite cross-feeding in syntrophic co-cultures can emerge from the accumulation of pathway intermediates and their conditional conversion under nutrient limitation, providing a plausible mechanism for the rapid establishment of mutualistic interactions. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: From Sparse Visits to Continuous Molecular Trajectories with Flow Matching
articles.abstract: Longitudinal transcriptomic studies often capture only a few molecular snapshots of each patient over time. This makes it challenging to understand how patients are progressing, compare them when progression rates differ, and capture molecular changes between observed visits. We introduce CohortFM, a flow-matching framework that reconstructs continuous patient-specific molecular trajectories from sparse longitudinal observations and organizes them through an integrated mixture model into a compact set of cohort-level progression patterns. CohortFM separates molecular progression from calendar time, places patients on a shared progression scale, uses observed intermediate states to guide the learned trajectories, and maps the resulting patterns back to real patient samples for biological interpretation. We evaluated CohortFM across COVID-19, sepsis, influenza, and tuberculosis. Despite different sampling patterns, the method generalizes well and consistently produces meaningful trajectories. These trajectories capture biological differences between patients that cannot be explained by the observed samples alone. Compared with state-of-the-art trajectory baselines, CohortFM produces more biologically distinct trajectories and a more complete representation of the patient population. Its finer progression scale also reveals biological programs and temporal dynamics that are not captured by visit-level analysis. We further evaluated interpolation and true forward prediction to test whether CohortFM can accurately recover unobserved states. CohortFM remains competitive with strong interpolation baselines and is among the strongest learned predictors in the harder forecasting setting. Ablation experiments further show that flow matching is the core learning mechanism and that our design choices improve continuous trajectory learning. Our results support CohortFM as a practical framework for turning sparse molecular snapshots into continuous, biologically interpretable trajectories. By going beyond visit labels, CohortFM makes it possible to study disease progression and predict future molecular states even when patients are sampled only a few times. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: HIV remodels germinal centers through T follicular helper cell loss
articles.abstract: T follicular helper cells (Tfh) within germinal centers are among the most permissive cells for HIV infection and serve as a critical part of the viral reservoir. Given the key role of Tfh in affinity maturation and the production of plasma cells and memory B cells, an understanding of this critical viral reservoir is fundamental not only for cure strategies but also for understanding immunodeficiency in people living with HIV (PLWH). Using rare clinical specimens from PLWH, we demonstrate that HIV causes both a change in the cellular composition of germinal centers and changes in their overall architecture in ways that are consistent with the immunodeficiency seen in PLWH, independent of their CD4 count. We note a significant decrease in the number of GC Tfh cells and an increase in the number of follicular CD8 T cells in lymphoid tissues obtained from PLWH. Our data further show that GC size is decreased both by HIV and with increased age. Single-cell RNA sequencing data demonstrate that HIV acutely decreases the expression of Tfh B-cell support pathways and disrupts Tfh expression of cell trafficking receptors. Additionally, in a lymphoid organoid model of acute infection that forms GC-like structures, these findings are recapitulated, suggesting that New Approach Methodologies could be germane to understanding the impact of HIV on the reservoir and immunodeficiency. This study describes previously undocumented remodeling of the germinal center niche in PLWH, providing insight into the immune microenvironment of a key HIV reservoir that may help inform future cure strategies.

articles.title: Identifying Network Factors Driving Changes in Brain Connectivity During Aging via Stochastic Actor-Oriented Models
articles.abstract: Brain network organization emerges from ongoing network dynamics that continuously create, maintain, and reorganize connectivity patterns. At both the structural and functional levels, these dynamics shape network evolution throughout the lifespan. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework based on Stochastic Actor-Oriented Models (SAOMs), which model longitudinal network changes as a process of local edge formation and dissolution driven by local-connectivity factors. Applied to functional and structural brain networks from an aging cohort, the resulting models recovered a set of interacting mechanisms that collectively promote hub formation, short-range connectivity, and modular organization. These factors were derived through a novel data-driven factor-selection procedure rather than specified a priori, allowing network mechanisms underlying longitudinal change to be identified directly from observations. Functional networks exhibited substantially higher rates of change than structural networks, suggesting more frequent opportunities for network maintenance and reorganization. Structural networks additionally showed despecification in the hub-forming mechanisms with cognitive impairment. These results support a view of brain network organization as an actively maintained process emerging from ongoing local connectivity dynamics. More broadly, this framework provides a general approach for studying longitudinal network dynamics through the estimation of network-generating mechanisms over time. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Research Council Canada, https://ror.org/04mte1k06, RGPIN-2022-03042, RGPIN-2023-03434 Canada Research Chairs, https://ror.org/0517h6h17

articles.title: Immunomodulatory RIG-I Agonist SLR14 Confers Protection Against a Range of Highly Pathogenic Negative Sense RNA viruses
articles.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging zoonotic RNA viruses, including filoviruses, henipaviruses and Rift Valley Fever virus (RVFV), pose a significant threat to human health. Due to their epidemic potential and high pathogenicity, these viruses are categorized as WHO priority pathogens, yet we still lack effective medical countermeasures (MCMs) against most of these dangerous pathogens, supporting that host-directed antivirals will be advantageous for broadly acting MCMs. Here we assessed the antiviral efficacy of SLR14, an immunomodulatory stem-loop RNA that activates RIG-I, for its activity against a panel of highly pathogenic viruses. SLR14 treatment provided broad-spectrum protection, markedly reducing infection with Ebola virus (EBOV), Marburg virus, and Sudan virus in human primary monocyte-derived macrophages, and Nipah virus replication in iPSC-derived endothelial cells, whether administered prophylactically or therapeutically. In vivo, a single dose of SLR14 protected mice against lethal RVFV infection when administered prophylactically, and, notably, retained significant efficacy when administered up to two days post-infection. Therapeutic SLR14 administration also improved survival rates of EBOV-infected mice. Although EBOV infection and SLR14 treatment activated overlapping innate immune pathways in human macrophages, viral infection induced a nonprotective response, whereas SLR14 elicited a well-regulated, markedly stronger and protective interferon-stimulated and inflammatory gene signature while avoiding prolonged IFN gene upregulation. Our data identify SLR14 as a potent host-directed therapeutic with broad antiviral efficacy against some of the most lethal viral pathogens. ### Competing Interest Statement A.M.P. is a co-founder and share-holder of RIGImmune. D.N.K. receives research grant support from GSK, unrelated to the current work. The other authors declare no conflict of interest. Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Emerging Pathogens Initiative Gates Foundation, https://ror.org/0456r8d26, INV-048926 National Institutes of Health, https://ror.org/01cwqze88, R01HL095993, P01HL170952, contract No. HHSN272201700041I, Intramural research program ZIA AI001254 NHLBI, 5K08HL173561 American Lung Association, https://ror.org/01p3rh655, Emerging Respiratory Pathogen Award

articles.title: Inferotemporal cortex stimulation is perceived before its onset
articles.abstract: Neural response latency measures when stimulus-evoked activity becomes detectable, but it does not reveal when the brain assigns the causal contribution of that activity to events in the external world. We define this temporal adjustment as projected delay and measure it in the macaque inferotemporal cortex using optogenetic stimulation and behavior. Two rhesus macaques performed a cortical perturbation detection task in which a visual masker appeared at different times relative to stimulation. Detection was selectively impaired when the masker began 200 ms before stimulation. We then tested this timing using Perceptography, a method that optimizes image perturbations to mimic stimulation-evoked visual events. Image perturbations presented 200 ms before stimulation elicited higher false-alarm rates than perturbations presented at stimulation onset. Here, we show that stimulation-evoked visual events in inferotemporal cortex depend preferentially on visual information originating approximately 200 ms before the cortical perturbation. This projected delay exceeds typical inferotemporal response latencies and suggests temporally extended readout mechanisms relevant to causal models of visual perception and the timing of cortical visual prostheses. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Intramural Research Program of the NIMH, ZIAMH002958

articles.title: Insights Into an Antibacterial Type VI Membrane-Disrupting Effector Of Adherent Invasive Escherichia coli
articles.abstract: Adherent Invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) strains are associated with ileal Crohn's disease and may contribute to intestinal dysbiosis through antibacterial competition. The AIEC reference strain LF82 encodes two type VI secretion systems (T6SSs), a contractile machine that injects an effector-loaded needle made of Hcp, VgrG and PAAR into neighbouring rivals, favoring niche colonization. LF82 T6SSs harbour several putative antibacterial toxin-immunity modules. Here we characterize the T6SS-1 encoded TmeAIEC, a PAAR-fused T6SS effector carrying a C-terminal Tme domain, hallmark of Tme (Type VI membrane disrupting effector) toxins, and its DUF1240-like immunity protein TmiAIEC. When heterologously produced in E. coli K-12 as well as in E. coli and Citrobacter clinical isolates, TmeAIEC is toxic only upon periplasmic targeting, and its toxicity is neutralized by TmiAIEC. Periplasmically-targeted TmeAIEC inserts into the inner membrane, collapses the proton motive force and increases cell permeability, consistent with a membrane-disrupting activity. Mutational analyses coupled to functional assays identified a predicted hydrophobic transmembrane segment and a conserved aspartate residue within the Tme domain as key determinants for TmeAIEC toxicity. These findings establish TmeAIEC/TmiAIEC as a functional T6SS toxin-immunity pair and reveal conserved determinants underlying the activity of Tme-family membrane-disrupting effectors. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Agence Nationale de la Recherche, https://ror.org/00rbzpz17, ANR-18-CE15-0013, 16-IDEX-0001 CAP 20-25

articles.title: Label-free identification of bacterial species using adapted vision transformers
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is an increasingly serious problem worldwide. Identifying the bacterial species can help guide antibiotic selection and improve patient outcomes. In sepsis, where every minute counts, rapid identification is particularly important, and new approaches are needed. In this study, deep learning models were trained to identify bacterial species from phase-contrast time-lapse images of cells growing in microfluidic traps, without fluorescent labels. We demonstrated this approach in two previous studies using laboratory strains. Here, the previous work is extended to clinical bacterial isolates, evaluating performance on isolates not seen during training. Furthermore, it was tested whether autofluorescence could aid species identification. Two validation sets were acquired in separate experiments from the training data, the first containing clinical-isolate traps with five species (Escherichia coli, Enterococcus faecalis, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus and Enterobacter cloacae), imaged every two minutes, and the second containing clinical isolates of two species (E. coli and K. pneumoniae) recovered from spiked donor blood, imaged every minute. Training with the best previous CNN method achieved unsatisfactory results. Therefore, vision transformers were explored, and a self-supervised adaptation procedure was developed for pretrained DINOv3 using a frozen teacher, followed by supervised classification using time-lapse montages. Mean macro-F1 was 93.6 ± 1.3% for isolates precultured in Mueller-Hinton medium using 60 frames (118 minutes) and 87.2 ± 2.7% for isolates precultured in blood using 55 frames (54 minutes) (mean ± sample standard deviation across training seeds). Performance was evaluated over time by increasing the number of frames available to the model during testing, and Fourier-domain filtering approximated reduced numerical aperture. The results are promising and suggest that the aperture can be decreased while retaining good results. However, further evaluation on independent isolates, experiments and patient samples is needed to establish generalization. Together with previous findings, these results bring us closer to rapid image-based diagnostics that could transform the initial treatment of acute bacterial infections by enabling better-informed antibiotic selection. ### Competing Interest Statement Johan Elf is a co-inventor on a patent for a microfluidic device used for antibiotic susceptibility testing (US10,041,104B2). He co-founded Astrego Diagnostics and Nornir Labs AB and is a shareholder of Nornir Labs AB. Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, ARC19-0016

articles.title: Metagenomic insights into dose-dependent alterations in the tobacco rhizosphere microbiome by pyrroloquinoline quinone
articles.abstract: Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is known to promote plant growth, yet how the rhizosphere microbiome varies with PQQ concentration remains poorly understood. We applied metagenomic sequencing to characterize the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the tobacco rhizosphere microbiome across PQQ treatments at 0.5, 1 and 2 μmol/L plus an untreated control. The rhizosphere microbiome was dominated by Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota and differed among treatments in a concentration-associated, non-monotonic manner. The most pronounced differences were observed at 1 μmol/L, where alpha diversity showed dimension-specific variation and beta-diversity analysis resolved the most distinct community profile. Taxonomic and functional profiles varied concurrently, with Streptomyces, Sphingomonas, Rhodanobacter and Lysobacter, together with functions related to biosynthesis, energy metabolism, colonization and environmental sensing, showing higher relative abundance at this concentration. No broad-spectrum antimicrobial effect was detected at the community level, and antibiotic resistance gene abundance showed no significant differences among treatments after correction for multiple testing. These findings provide a basis for further evaluation of PQQ in modulating the rhizosphere microbiome in continuous cropping systems.

articles.title: Non-canonical alternate interactors of SARS CoV-2 Spike protein implicated in placental susceptibilty
articles.abstract: Vertical transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is controversial. Owing to the low expression of ACE2 along with TMPRSS2 in placenta, role of secondary receptors becomes significant. In our study we predicted twelve interactors of spike protein expressed in placenta through interactome analysis followed by docking and molecular dynamic simulation. Three interactors of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein were found to be CD147, EGFR and LDLR. Expression at transcriptomic and translational level by real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry respectively was observed in placenta samples obtained from women with COVID exposure risk and compared to control. Elevated protein levels of CD147 (OR=14.667), ACE2 (OR=8.25) and LDLR (OR=1.9) was associated with higher exposure risk. However, the variation in mRNA expression was not statistically significant. Computational study showed that CD147/basigin, EGFR and LDLR stably interact with spike protein outside its primary receptor binding domain. In-vitro binding assay confirmed the physical interaction between spike protein and the placental receptors. In-silico site-directed mutagenesis further identified key potential binding hotspots of spike protein- Tyr28 and Trp64 for CD147, Phe643, Val642, Thr632 for LDLR and Leu8, Phe59, Phe32, Tyr28, Trp64, Trwp152, His245, and Val213 for EGFR. Finally, concluded that CD147, EGFR and LDLR might act as secondary non-canonical cofactors for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in placenta, thereby increasing its susceptibility and tissue tropism. The study overall gives a better insight into potential placental suscpetibility providing targeted therapeutic opportunities.

articles.title: Photostimulus intensity, rather than colour or polarization, is the key driver for stable fly visual attraction in laboratory bioassays
articles.abstract: Foraging hematophagous flies such as the stable fly, Stomoxys calcitrans , are shown or expected to sense multiple characteristics of visual host cues. These include relative intensity, spectral composition, and the angle and degree of polarization. Here, we investigated the role of each of these visual cue characteristics on stable fly attraction. In laboratory two-choice bioassays, we offered groups of female or male stable flies a choice between paired photostimuli that differed in their visual characteristics, recording the flies' landing responses on stimuli as the response criterion. Bioassay flies preferentially selected lower-intensity visual stimuli even when paired stimuli markedly differed in spectral composition and polarization characteristics (a high degree of horizontal or vertical polarization). When paired stimuli had identical relative intensity, flies failed to discriminate between the stimulus that presented ultraviolet, blue, green, and red wavebands and a corresponding paired stimulus lacking one of these wavebands. Our results support the hypothesis that foraging stable flies may respond to colour and polarization characteristics of visual stimuli as modulations of perceived intensity. Acquired knowledge on the mechanisms that underlie stable fly visual attraction may inform the design of vision-based traps so that they become optimally attractive to stable flies and other biting flies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Point-Process Modelling of Cell-Type Interaction Structure in CosMx Glioma Data for Hypothesis-Driven Tumor Inference from scRNA-seq
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits marked spatial heterogeneity that is lost after tissue dissociation for single–cell RNA sequencing. Here, we developed a spatial–statistical framework to characterize tumor–microenvironment organization and derive molecularly predictable spatial phenotypes from CosMx data. Eight GBM specimens comprising 2,427,362 cells, 15 cell populations, and four malignant states were analyzed, revealing substantial inter–patient differences in cellular composition and density. Fine finite–element meshes best preserved continuous spatial intensity and supported whole–tissue Log–Gaussian Cox Process modelling. Immune populations, including macrophages, microglia, monocytes, cDCs, neutrophils, and T cells, showed spatial attraction toward malignant states. These models generated cell–level measures of conditional intensity and tumor–proximity probability. Transcript abundances and metabolic pathway scores served as the sole predictive features to model these spatial phenotypes. Transcriptomic representations outperformed metabolic pathway scores. Leave–one–patient–out validation reduced predictive performance, and patient–wise harmonization failed to restore cross–patient transportability. Spatial outcome distributions varied between specimens, indicating that molecular–spatial relationships are strongly conditioned by patient-specific tumor architecture. Predicted interaction scores stratified transcriptional subclusters within cell types in external non–spatial single-cell datasets. This framework links spatial point–process phenotypes to molecular states and provides a basis for inferring spatial context from non–spatial single–cell data. Generalizing these models requires larger and more diverse spatial cohorts. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP), #2025/15993-2, #2025/26980-9, #2025/17477-1, #2018/00583-0

articles.title: Pooled progeny sequencing effectively estimates polyandry in species with large families
articles.abstract: Polyandry, multiple mating by females, both benefits females by increases genetic variation within families and provides an opportunity for sexual selection through sperm competition and cryptic female choice. Estimating polyandry in species with large clutches is challenging because genotyping all progeny individually can be impractical. We present a likelihood-based framework for estimating the number of sires and their relative contributions from the maternal genotype and pooled sequencing of entire progeny pools. The method evaluates the probability of observed pooled offspring read counts under alternative paternal genotype mixtures, accounting for Mendelian segregation and sampling variation from finite sequencing depth. We implement this framework for both biallelic SNPs and short-read mini-haplotype markers constructed from closely linked SNPs, which provide multi-allelic information comparable to traditional microsatellite markers. Simulations show that this approach accurately recovers sire number and sire contributions across a range of conditions. We then applied the method to 275 wild-caught Drosophila melanogaster females and their offspring from a Kansas population using 3,053 biallelic SNPs and 239 four-allele mini-haplotype markers. Estimates from the two marker sets were highly concordant, and combined analyses indicate that 57% of families were sired by a single male. These results demonstrate that pooled progeny sequencing provides an efficient genomic approach for estimating polyandry in species with large families. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. U.S. National Science Foundation, IOS-2421689

articles.title: Predicted structure of the 89-kDa invasion-tip protein of Holospora obtusa, an endonuclear symbiont of Paramecium caudatum, suggests a pH-dependent conformational change
articles.abstract: The endonuclear symbiont Holospora obtusa invades the macronucleus of Paramecium caudatum using an infectious-form invasion-tip containing a major 89-kDa periplasmic protein implicated in escape from the host digestive vacuole and macronuclear invasion. Sequence-based analyses placed this protein within a Holospora-specific family and predicted an N-terminal membrane-anchoring module and a long alpha-helical C-terminal region. AlphaFold2 modeling followed by molecular dynamics indicated that the C-terminal region forms an antiparallel, spectrin-repeat-like helical solenoid containing a localized three-helix coiled-coil. The protein exhibits a large pH-dependent charge difference, becoming 55 units more positive at pH 4 than at pH 7. Independent simulations at these pH values differed mainly in the relative orientation of the N-terminal core and C-terminal rod, described by DynDom as an approximately 35 degrees rigid-body rotation about a hinge centered on Gly291. However, none of the nearby glutamates (Glu273, Glu275, and Glu302) formed a pH-dependent salt bridge, and no specific protonation-dependent interaction responsible for the conformational difference was identified. We nonetheless propose, as a testable hypothesis, that acidification of the digestive vacuole may promote this reorientation, thereby repositioning the N-terminal membrane-anchoring module at the bacterial surface as an early step toward escape from the vacuole. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Restoration of deficient IL-15 signaling enhances innate lymphoid cell immunity in brain metastasis
articles.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells and type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s), collectively known as group 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILCs), are critical mediators of anti-tumor immunity, yet their role in brain metastasis remains poorly defined. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and functional depletion models, we show that group 1 ILCs fail to provide adequate tumor control in breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM). In contrast to the liver, where diverse, functionally competent group 1 ILC populations facilitate excellent metastatic control, group 1 ILCs in BCBM show limited diversity and profound tissue-specific dysfunction such that their depletion had no effect on tumor burden despite modest parenchymal infiltration. We attribute this group 1 ILC dysfunction to severely restricted IL-15 availability, with IL-15Rα protein detected at 500-fold lower concentration in the brain than in the liver. Local IL-15 complex administration restored group 1 ILC accumulation, cytotoxicity, and tissue residency, significantly reducing brain metastatic burden independent of T cells. Intracranial delivery of IL-15-secreting induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived (iPSC)-NK cells, already in clinical testing for non-small cell lung cancer, significantly reduced tumor burden. Collectively, these findings reveal how tissue-specific differences in cytokine availability shape group 1 ILC population diversity and disease response, establishing localized IL-15 signaling as a compelling strategy to unlock innate immunity against intracranial malignancies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. California Institute for Regenerative Medicine (CIRM), TRAN1-14003, DISC2-14190, EDUC4-12822 Team Michelle & Friends UCI SCRC Pilot Grant George E. Hewitt Foundation for Medical Research Canadian Institutes of Health Research Postdoctoral Fellowship Mike and Suzette Kirby Foundation, R01CA237376-01A, 1P01CA288662-01A1, 1T32GM154637-01, 1K99CA267160-01, R01AI174519, R01AI186079 Anti-Cancer Challenge Pilot Grant Emerging Leader Award from the Mark Foundation for Cancer Research Mike and Suzette Kirby Foundation Anti-Cancer Challenge Pilot Grant

articles.title: RiboFlow v2: a configurable ribosome profiling pipeline reveals measurements sensitive to read-mapping methodology
articles.abstract: Ribosome profiling experiments capture a snapshot of translation by sequencing ribosome-protected fragments (RPFs). Alignment to a well-curated transcriptome captures most RPF signal, but can miss ribosome activity when expressed exons are absent from the reference. Genome alignment of RPFs expands the detectable sequence space, but can expose ambiguity between homologous loci. Existing workflows often couple reference choice with the handling of ambiguously mapped reads, making it difficult to isolate the effects of either decision on downstream analyses. Here, we developed RiboFlow v2 by adding genome alignment and configurable handling of multimapping reads to the existing transcriptome workflow. Using 24 human ribosome profiling libraries and their matched RNA-seq data, we found that nucleotide-level coverage at matched coding-sequence positions and translation efficiency (TE) were broadly concordant between alignment strategies under stringent alignment filters. Even under these conditions, individual genes showed substantial differences in coverage and TE estimates. These differences included coverage in alternative exons absent from selected transcripts and ambiguous alignments between protein-coding genes and processed pseudogenes. Clustering genes by read-assignment patterns identified groups associated with pseudogene prevalence and highlighted shared exonic sequence among reference transcripts as a source of alignment discrepancies. RiboFlow v2 extends the analysis beyond selected reference transcripts and enables identification of genes whose ribosome coverage and abundance estimates depend on reference composition and how ambiguously mapped reads are handled. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Welch Foundation, F-2027-20260402 NIGMS, R35GM150667

articles.title: Staphylococcus aureus GpsB, Stk, and VraSR form a cell wall surveillance network to maintain cell envelope integrity and mediate antibiotic resistance
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is an alarming threat to public health worldwide. Specifically, drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus remains a major contributor to global mortality. Therefore, in-depth understanding of antibiotic resistance mechanisms is urgently needed to inform alternative therapeutic strategies. We previously showed that GpsB is a critical regulator of cell wall synthesis in S. aureus. GpsB executes its regulatory role via protein-protein interactions. Yet, how GpsB function is modulated in this organism has remained unclear. Intriguingly, a prior proteomics report indicated that GpsB is phosphorylated at six different residues by the sole serine/threonine kinase Stk. Hence, we explored the physiological significance of GpsB phosphorylation. We identify three phosphosites that are each independently sufficient to drive GpsB phosphoregulation, which likely alters its partner preference. We find that cells lacking gpsB exhibit heightened fosfomycin sensitivity, and that this is exacerbated by stk deletion. Our findings reveal that GpsB collaborates with Stk and the VraSR cell wall stress response system to coordinate the demand-driven availability of cell wall precursors. Collectively, this report establishes GpsB as a pivotal peptidoglycan supply chain sentinel that together with Stk and VraSR forms an integrated cell wall stress monitoring network that maintains cell envelope homeostasis and aids in antibiotic resistance. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institute of General Medical Sciences, https://ror.org/04q48ey07, R35GM133617 University of South Florida, https://ror.org/032db5x82, Center for Antimicrobial Resistance Award

articles.title: Systematic benchmark of demultiplexing workflows for direct RNA sequencing
articles.abstract: Direct RNA nanopore sequencing offers the capacity to directly profile native RNAs, enabling detection of diverse epitranscriptomic modifications based on current changes as the RNA passes through a pore. Innovations in chemistry, hardware and bioinformatic tools have increased sequencing capacity and accuracy, creating demand for sequencing multiple samples within individual runs. Two recent solutions enable barcoding and demultiplexing of samples, but independent comparisons of their performance is limited. Here we benchmark WarpDemuX and SeqTagger using orthogonal ground truths derived from species identity and matched IVT spike-ins across four RNA004 flow cells. Both achieve high demultiplexing precision but differ in their trade-offs in precision and retention. SeqTagger provided strong performance at its recommended settings, whilst WarpDemuX performance varied by model, barcode and read quality. IVT-derived score cutoffs allowed dataset-specific calibration and increased WarpDeMux assignment yield, although precision achieved on IVTs was not consistently reproduced in species reads. These results support matched IVTs as internal controls for guiding choice of demultiplexing settings, while demonstrating the need to validate demultiplexing precision in biological RNA populations. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Novo Nordisk Foundation, https://ror.org/04txyc737, NNF24SA0092867 Lundbeck Foundation, R436-2023-1176 Villum Fonden, https://ror.org/05nqkay65, VIL58880

articles.title: Targeted Depletion of rRNAs and Tobamoviruses Enhances Viral Discovery in Wastewater Metatranscriptomes
articles.abstract: Wastewater contains a complex mixture of nucleic acids derived from human cells, microorganisms, diets, and agricultural or industrial inputs. Metatranscriptomics has the potential to broaden the understanding of wastewater viromes, but its utility is constrained by high-abundance RNA molecules that prevent the detection of lower-abundance signals, including human pathogens. Two major sources of this interfering background signal are ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs) from various organisms, and plant-infecting tobamoviruses from human diets, which are often the most abundant RNA viruses in wastewater. These rRNA molecules and RNA genomes can account for upwards of 95% of total RNA sequences, thereby obscuring the detection of lower-abundance viruses of public health importance. This study evaluated whether combined depletion of ribosomal RNAs and genomic RNA from abundant plant tobamoviruses can improve the recovery of underrepresented viral sequences from wastewater. RNA extracts from a large municipal wastewater treatment plant in Calgary, Canada, were processed with or without probe-based depletion of rRNAs and eight abundant tobamoviruses. Metatranscriptomes revealed that depletion reduced rRNA reads by 90%. Reads assigned to tobamoviruses, which accounted for up to 25% of viral reads in untreated samples, were reduced to <2% of viral reads after depletion. This decrease in undesired RNA signal led to an order of magnitude increase in viral read signals and improved assembled viral genome quality. Furthermore, the number of reads assigned to human and animal pathogens increased 42-fold after depletion, enabling the detection of important pathogens like influenza, RSV, and hepatitis A, which were undecteable in untreated samples. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeted depletion of abundant background RNAs improves the detection of low abundance viruses, and enhances the utility of metatranscriptomic approaches for wastewater viral surveillance. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council, https://ror.org/01h531d29, ALLRP 597320-24

articles.title: The porin MspA is a phage-specific determinant of mycobacteriophage infection
articles.abstract: Mycobacteriophages are being developed as therapeutics for mycobacterial infections, but their highly variable host ranges limit this application and the bacterial factors that determine whether infection succeeds remain poorly defined. The determinants characterized so far are dominated by cell envelope lipids and glycolipids. Here, we performed a genome-wide CRISPRi screen in Mycobacterium smegmatis to identify host functions associated with susceptibility to BPsΔ33HTH HRM10. After prolonged phage challenge, the outer membrane porin genes mspA and mspC were among the most strongly enriched hits, whereas the closely related paralogs mspB and mspD were not enriched despite sharing high amino-acid identity across the family. Deletion of mspA or mspC reduced BPsΔ33HTH HRM10 plaque formation and produced smaller, more turbid plaques, with the stronger phenotype following loss of mspA, the major outer membrane porin of M. smegmatis. Across a panel of 25 mycobacteriophages, 11 showed either a more than tenfold reduction in titer or loss of discrete plaque formation on ΔmspA, while the remainder were largely unaffected. These findings identify outer membrane porins as phage-dependent determinants of mycobacterial susceptibility, revealing an additional layer of specificity in phage infection beyond previously characterized cell envelope lipids and glycolipids. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, https://ror.org/004hzzk67, 2020.0239 Swedish Research Council, https://ror.org/03zttf063, 2023-01970

articles.title: The transition to postpartum lactation establishes a state of maternal antiviral resilience
articles.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) causes severe disease during late pregnancy, yet how maternal adaptations in host defense shape susceptibility following childbirth remains unknown. Here, we show that the postpartum period represents a state of enhanced maternal antiviral immunity. Across postpartum stages, dams infected before weaning exhibited increased survival and reduced disease following lethal IAV challenge compared with nonpregnant females. Postpartum protection was associated with enhanced viral clearance and increased pulmonary antigen-specific CD8+ T cells and IL-17A-producing gamma-delta T cells. We identify the transition into lactation as a critical determinant of this protection. Protection extended to highly pathogenic avian influenza. Together, these findings reveal that maternal antiviral immunity remains actively shaped after childbirth, establishing the postpartum lactational period as a distinct state of maternal antiviral resilience. ### Competing Interest Statement KK and PS are co-inventors on a patent relating to this work. KK and PS are co-founders of Coralie Bio, Inc. that may benefit financially from the work described in this article. National Institutes of Health, https://ror.org/01cwqze88, 1R01HD120540, 1F31AI191458 David and Lucile Packard Foundation, https://ror.org/032atxq54, Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering U.S. National Science Foundation, https://ror.org/021nxhr62, Graduate Research Fellowship Program Howard Hughes Medical Institute, https://ror.org/006w34k90, Gilliam Fellowship Program Blavatnik Family Foundation, Blavatnik Biomedical Accelerator at Harvard University Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering

articles.title: TonB-dependent Transporters of Fe-petrobactin in Marinobacter nauticus and Southern Ocean bacteria
articles.abstract: TonB-dependent transporters (TBDTs) play a central role in siderophore-mediated iron acquisition in the marine environment. However, assigning substrate specificity to TBDTs remains a major bottleneck in understanding the ecological and mechanistic roles of siderophore production and uptake. Here, we identify in Marinobacter nauticus two TBDTs, OptA and OptB, that share low sequence identity yet both mediate Fe-petrobactin uptake. Despite this functional overlap, they underlie distinct regulatory mechanisms, suggesting differential utilization under specific environmental conditions. Phylogenetic analyses indicate that OptA likely co-evolved with the petrobactin biosynthetic gene cluster, whereas OptB appears to have followed a distinct evolutionary trajectory, acquiring the capacity to import petrobactin as a xenosiderophore. Using resuscitated communities from the Southern Ocean, we further show that Fe-petrobactin stimulated prokaryotic growth. Based on amino acid similarity, we identified OptB-like transporters encoded in metagenomes and MAGs and show that taxa harbouring these transporters, such as Pseudoaltermonas, respond specifically to Fe-petrobactin addition. OptB-like transporters were also detected in environmental metagenomes from the Southern Ocean, whereas the petrobactin biosynthetic gene clusters were not, indicating that petrobactin primarily functions as a xenosiderophore in natural communities. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Agence Nationale de la Recherche, ANR19-CE01-0012, ANR EDIR-22-0005, ANR 17-EURE-0015 CNRS - MITI interdisciplinary programs CNRS - LEFE actions Université de Pau et des Pays de l'Adour, https://ror.org/01frn9647, MeSMic

articles.title: Transcription factor interactions promote binding to non-cognate DNA sites
articles.abstract: Recruitment of transcription factors (TFs) to non-cognate DNA sequences is widely observed, but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that, within the nucleosome, Sox2 can bind an Oct4 motif, interact with the Oct4 POU-specific domain, and displace the Oct4 homeodomain. We also observe Sox2 binding at multiple near-canonical and non-canonical DNA sites, with these interactions promoted by a second Sox2 molecule or by nearby nucleosome-bound Oct4. The TF-TF interactions can bridge across DNA gyres, bringing together binding sites that are distant in linear DNA but spatially proximal on the nucleosome. We further find that Sox2 can engage across nucleosomal DNA gyres through loop regions and/or intrinsically disordered segments, providing an additional mode of chromatin binding. Together, our structural and biochemical data reveal how TF-TF interactions change DNA recognition on the nucleosome, enabling binding to non-cognate sequences and expanding the repertoire of pioneer factor interactions on chromatin. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institute of General Medical Sciences, https://ror.org/04q48ey07, R35GM158165.

articles.title: Transcriptomics uncovers outer membrane remodeling as conserved strategy for Burkholderia cenocepacia survival in protozoan and macrophage phagosomes
articles.abstract: Bacterivorous protists expose bacteria to hostile stress conditions that resemble those encountered within macrophage phagosomes and may therefore act as training grounds for bacterial pathogens. However, the mechanisms enabling bacterial survival within protozoan phagosomes remain poorly understood. Here we characterized the transcriptome of the opportunistic pathogen Burkholderia cenocepacia during transit through phagosomes and expelled food vacuoles of the ubiquitous protozoan ciliate Tetrahymena elliotti. Our data revealed a coordinated response involving bacterial metabolic reprogramming, with the upregulation of NADPH-generating pathways and host nutrient uptake systems, alongside the activation of several stress responses and envelope remodeling to maintain outer membrane barrier function and repair phagosomal damage. Disruption of antioxidant defenses, the RpoE-dependent envelope stress response, the Mla pathway and other proteins required for outer membrane integrity severely impaired intracellular survival in both protozoa and macrophages, revealing conserved mechanisms required for persistence within evolutionarily distant phagocytes. This adaptive response not only contributed to survival but it also primed B. cenocepacia for increased chlorhexidine resistance and adhesion to collagen and human lung epithelial cells. Collectively, our findings reveal that protozoan phagosomes drive physiological adaptations with consequences extending beyond grazing resistance. Protozoa may therefore disseminate stress-adapted bacteria with enhanced resistance and colonization potential, providing a mechanistic link between adaptation to environmental predators and survival in the human host. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Spanish Sate Research Agency, Ministry of Science and Innovation, PID2020-113540GB-I00, PDI2024-157739NB-I00

articles.title: Type 6 secretion systems of adherent-invasive Escherichia coli isolated from Crohn's disease patients shape intestinal microbiota.
articles.abstract: Adherent Invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) colonize the ileal mucosa of Crohn's disease patients. Among bacterial virulence factors potentially implicated, type 6 secretion systems (T6SS) are molecular machineries sending effectors in prokaryotic or eukaryotic target cells. Two T6SS have been reported in AIEC LF82 reference strain. Here, we show that T6SS genes are more prevalent in Crohn's disease patients' microbiota compared to healthy controls, and that T6SS are more frequent in AIEC pathovar compared to E. coli in general and associated with FimH pathoadaptive polymorphism. The use of an in vitro gastrointestinal system coupled with T6SS promoter reporter assay highlighted expression of LF82 T6SS under gastrointestinal conditions, with a major role for bile salts. In mice infected with AIEC LF82 versus T6SS-deleted mutants, T6SS showed a functional impact in modulating the composition of mucosa-associated gut microbiota. Thus, AIEC may use their T6SS to compete with endogenous microbiota to colonize host mucosa. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Urban Vietnam at the microbiome transition: Co-existing enterotypes reflect the global industrialization patterns
articles.abstract: Vietnam's rapid socioeconomic and dietary transition offers a rare window into how industrialization is reflected in the gut microbiome, yet Vietnamese populations remain underrepresented in global reference datasets. We investigated whether healthy Vietnamese adults in Hanoi harbor microbial community configurations associated with different stages of industrialization. Metagenomic data from stool samples of 183 clinically screened participants in Hanoi were analyzed alongside 629 publicly available metagenomic datasets from populations in low to middle income (LMI) and high income (HI) countries. Species-level taxonomic composition and gene-content-based metabolic pathways were characterized using community clustering and multivariable association analyses. Rather than forming a single population profile, the Vietnamese cohort separated into two enterotypes that mirrored the global industrialization gradient. Enterotype 1 more closely resembled populations from LMICs and showed greater microbial richness and diversity, whereas Enterotype 2 aligned with taxonomic and functional profiles observed in HICs. Both taxonomic and functional potential shows similar trajectories. Diet and lifestyle patterns describe some of the variance between enterotypes, supporting an association between contemporary exposures and microbiome structure without establishing causation. Antibiotic resistance profiles also varied between enterotypes, suggesting that the transition may encompass functions relevant to antimicrobial exposure. Together, these findings position urban Vietnam at a microbiome transition, where community states associated with different levels of industrialization coexist within a single population. This Vietnamese reference cohort expands representation in global metagenomic research and provides a baseline for tracking how rapid socioeconomic change may reshape microbial ecology, metabolic capacity, and antimicrobial resistance. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Vinmec-VinUni Institute of Immunology, Grant 23.11.SRI

articles.title: Using the aperiodic slope across learning to predict sleep-based memory consolidation
articles.abstract: Homeostatic mechanisms adjust synaptic strengths to regulate neuronal activity across wake-sleep cycles. Although sleep supports memory consolidation, limited research has explored how sleep-induced homeostatic changes influence memory outcomes in humans. The EEG-derived aperiodic slope (1/f) could be a candidate measure of homeostatic memory processes through its reflection of neural excitation-inhibition balance. In this study, 27 participants learned object-word pairs, and completed an immediate recognition test before either a nap or equivalent wakeful period. Resting-state EEG was recorded, both before and after learning and the interval, to derive changes in aperiodic slope values. A delayed recognition test then assessed whether changes in the aperiodic slope (i.e., homeostatic activity) across learning and the interval predicted memory accuracy and N400 amplitude, an index of stimulus expectancy and recognition. Our study found evidence to suggest homeostatic renormalisation, for the nap condition only, indicated by a shift towards inhibition across sleep which was inversely related to the slope change across learning. Although the aperiodic slope change across the nap and wake intervals did not predict delayed memory accuracy, a shift towards inhibition during learning was beneficial for memory accuracy, only in the nap condition. Similarly, a shift towards inhibition across learning, followed by a shift towards excitation in the nap condition, predicted reduced N400 amplitudes. This suggests that homeostatic renormalisation across the nap influenced model updating and stimulus expectancy. This study provides evidence for a link between synaptic homeostatic processes and memory consolidation, emphasising the importance of encoding-related aperiodic activity in this relationship. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Water Kefir as a Model for Aggregative Development of Microbial Multicellularity within a Multispecies Biofilm
articles.abstract: Water kefir is a traditional fermented beverage and a non-dairy alternative to milk kefir. Water kefir grains are cauliflower-like aggregates, ranging in size from 1-20 mm. They are composed of an exopolysaccharide matrix derived from the fermentation substrate sucrose. The microbial community on and within the grains is a complex, highly stable multicellular aggregate typically consisting of 10-15 core species that primarily belong to three major groups: lactic acid bacteria, acetic acid bacteria, and yeasts. Remarkably, the structural organisation, stability, and growth of kefir grains cannot be readily explained by their constituent species alone, and attempts to reconstitute them from the isolated species have so far been unsuccessful. Here, we combined a comprehensive structural investigation of the macro- and micromorphology of water kefir grains with culture-dependent and -independent analyses of its microbial biodiversity. The dynamics and interactions within this complex microbial community were studied by combining flow cytometry, fluorescence-activated cell sorting, and amplicon sequencing of selected subpopulations. Furthermore, the growth of water kefir grains was spatiotemporally resolved and quantitatively characterised, thereby unravelling an emergent multicellular growth function, documented for the first time. Our combined evidence provides an unprecedented understanding of a highly structured and metabolically synergistic multicellular microbial aggregate and lets us propose water kefir as a model system for the aggregative development of microbial multicellularity from multiple species. It should lay the foundation for future mechanistic studies aimed at understanding how multispecies microbial communities self-organise into stable, spatially structured multicellular aggregates. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft, https://ror.org/018mejw64, 504017689, 503905203

articles.title: Widespread attraction of marine bacteria to the macroalgae-derived polysaccharide fucoidan
articles.abstract: Fucoidan is the second most abundant polysaccharide in brown macroalgae, contributing up to 50% of the dissolved organic matter released daily from these algae into the ocean, substantially influencing the marine carbon cycle. Due to its complex chemical structure, fucoidan is highly resistant to microbial degradation and accumulates on the surface of macroalgae, where it contributes to regulating their microbiome. Here, we used a range of microfluidic assays to quantify the chemotactic and physiological responses of marine bacteria to fucoidan. Our results reveal that all the strains tested (14 out of 14) are attracted to fucoidan produced by two different species of brown macroalgae. Attraction occurred only at high fucoidan concentrations (0.1 to 1 mg/mL), such as those expected in the immediate vicinity of algal surfaces, whereas low concentrations elicited no response or modest chemorepulsion. Although fucoidan did not support bacterial growth under our experimental conditions, it did not impair the utilization of other carbon sources. Together, these findings suggest that fucoidan gradients can act as chemical cues guiding marine bacteria toward the nutrient-rich microenvironment of macroalgal surfaces, pointing to a potential ecological role of fucoidan in shaping macroalgal microbiota, bacterial behavior, and ultimately carbon cycling in the ocean. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Swiss National Science Foundation, https://ror.org/00yjd3n13 Simons Foundation, https://ror.org/01cmst727

articles.title: Winnow-tax: sensitive and precise taxonomic profiling of low-coverage organisms in shotgun metagenomes
articles.abstract: Accurate species-level profiling of shotgun metagenomes becomes difficult when an organism is represented by only sparse sequence coverage. Per-read k-mer classifiers can retain sensitivity under these conditions, but short reads from conserved or shared genomic regions can generate false-positive calls among closely related references. More conservative marker-gene and genome-containment approaches generally provide stronger species-level specificity but may lose sensitivity as genomic sampling becomes sparse. We present winnow-tax, a two-stage taxonomic profiling pipeline that separates sensitive candidate nomination from genome-level confirmation. Candidate species are nominated using Sylph, Kraken2, and a branch-rescue procedure, then reads are competitively recruited to a sample-specific reference set. Species presence is evaluated using read support, observed genome breadth, and a Lander-Waterman-based breadth ratio that compares observed breadth with the breadth expected at the measured mean depth. In a controlled synthetic community of 82 genomes with human DNA background, winnow-tax maintained a stronger precision-sensitivity balance than Kraken2/Bracken, Sylph, and MetaPhlAn 4 as genome coverage decreased, with its advantage concentrated near the low-coverage detection boundary. In the CAMI III Toy Longitudinal Human Gut benchmark, winnow-tax had higher sensitivity than Sylph (0.803 versus 0.672), lower precision (0.923 versus 0.970), and a modestly but significantly higher F1 score (0.858 versus 0.793). In a clinical enteric stool cohort with culture/PCR reference testing, winnow-tax achieved the best composite performance for Salmonella, detecting 37 of 48 composite-positive samples with one false-positive call. Together, these results support a profiling strategy in which weak taxonomic signals are retained during candidate generation but require genomic evidence distributed as broadly as expected for their sequencing depth before species presence is accepted.

articles.title: Crystal Phase-Dependent Electronic Metal-Support Interactions Enable Chemoselective Hydrogenation of α, β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
articles.abstract: Electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) provide an effective means of tuning the electronic structure of supported metal catalysts and thereby modulating their catalytic properties. However, how the crystal phase of supports governs EMSI and in turn influences the selective hydrogenation remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a crystal-phase engineering strategy to precisely regulate EMSI in ultrafine Ir nanoclusters (NCs) supported on polymorphic Nb2O5. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization reveals that the orthorhombic Nb2O5-T phase forms a distinctive socketed metal-support interface that strongly anchors Ir NCs and induces substantial electron transfer from the support to the metal. Distinct from classical strong metal-support interactions that often compromise active-site accessibility, this socketed interfacial configuration simultaneously enhances EMSI, stabilizes the Ir NCs, and preserves abundant exposed active sites. The resulting electron-rich Ir species facilitates H2 activation and interfacial hydrogen spillover while favoring preferential adsorption of the carbonyl group over the C=C bond in α, β-unsaturated aldehydes. Consequently, Ir@Nb2O5-T exhibits high activity, selectivity, and durability for the selective hydrogenation to unsaturated alcohols under mild conditions, overcoming the typical activity–selectivity trade-off. This work establishes a direct crystal phase–EMSI–reactivity relationship and highlights crystal-phase engineering as a powerful strategy for manipulating metal–support interfaces toward highly selective heterogeneous catalysis.

articles.title: Engineering the Interfacial Microenvironment to Boost Ethane Dehydrogenation on Ga2O3-Pt Catalysts via Metal Doping Modulation
articles.abstract: Inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts have exhibited better catalytic performance in propane dehydrogenation due to their tunable interfacial electronic properties. This study explores the potential of inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts and their single-atom-doped variant (Ga2O3-M/Pt) systems for ethane dehydrogenation using DFT calculations and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. The results show that Ga2O3-Pt exhibits low ethylene formation activity (0.83 × 102 s–1) and selectivity (84.28%) due to its interfacial sites that weakly and uniformly adsorb hydrogen, impeding the differential regulation of key CH2CH3* intermediate adsorption behavior. Single-atom doping (M = Ti, Co, etc.) creates a Pt–M–O interfacial microenvironment, modulating the electronic structure of interfacial oxygen sites, which enables the effective differential regulation of CH2CH3* intermediate adsorption, thereby enhancing catalytic performance. Among the 14 screened dopants, the Ga2O3-Ti/Pt catalyst emerged as optimal, showing high activity (2.86 × 103 s–1) and selectivity (97.13%) for ethylene formation at the optimal 873.15 K and CH3CH3(g) partial pressure of 0.20 bar. This advantage stems from its moderate p-band center and Ti–O charge transfer, which yield an ideal hydrogen adsorption energy for CH2CH3* regulation. The H* adsorption energy can serve as a descriptor for qualitatively evaluating the activity of CH2CH2(g) formation for a series of Ga2O3-M/Pt catalysts. This work proposes the strategy of “interfacial microenvironment reconstruction to regulate the electronic structure” as a design method for developing high-efficiency alkane dehydrogenation catalysts.

articles.title: Enhanced Aqueous-Phase Hydrodeoxygenation of Fatty Acids over CoP Anchored on P–N Co-Doped Carbon
articles.abstract: The aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of biomass-derived fatty acids offers an alternative route for the production of diesel-range hydrocarbons, but remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a hydrophobic CoP catalyst anchored on P–N co-doped carbon spheres (CoP@PNC-900), which exhibits high performance for the aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of palmitic acid at 270 °C and 2 MPa H2, delivering nearly complete conversion together with over 99% yield of C15+C16 alkanes.
