Belowground growth is the primary driver of radial oxygen loss from Typha angustifolia to sediment
articles.abstract: Oxygen pool accompanying the growth of a new Typha angustifolia rhizome through anoxic sediment. Summary Wetland plants must supply oxygen to their rhizomes and roots to maintain aerobic respiration despite soil anoxia. Excess oxygen can diffuse into the environment, strongly affecting rhizosphere biogeochemistry. This radial oxygen loss (ROL) has often been observed to increase in the daytime, perhaps supported by photosynthetic oxygen production and stomatal opening. However, dynamics in rhizosphere oxygen pools do not derive exclusively from diel cycles. Using oxygen‐sensitive planar optodes (and simultaneous leaf gas exchange measurements), we compared the timing and magnitude of variation in rhizosphere oxygen pools due to diel cycles vs root and rhizome development in the widespread aquatic macrophyte Typha angustifolia. Diel cycles drove only slight variation in oxygen pool sizes (c. 5% oxygen saturation). Strongly oxygenated regions – regularly 25–30% oxygen saturation – appeared as roots and rhizomes grew, and then disappeared after several days of maturation. Expansive plumes of oxygen also developed upon the emergence of lateral roots and persisted for several weeks. These results indicate that root and rhizome development are dominant determinants of ROL in T. angustifolia. Seasonal and environmental controls over timing of belowground development likely have strong implications for rhizosphere biogeochemistry ranging from microbe‐controlled decomposition to redox‐sensitive transformation of metals in natural and managed systems.

articles.title: The ABCG transporter OsPDR17 mediates transport of 5,10‐diketo‐casbene and enhances disease resistance in rice
articles.abstract: Working model for the mechanism by which OsPDR17‐mediated transport of 5,10‐diketo‐casbene contributes to resistance against bacterial blight in shoots. Summary Compound 5,10‐diketo‐casbene (DKC) is a key macrocyclic diterpenoid phytoalexin contributing to rice resistance against bacterial blight. Although its activity depends on transmembrane transport, the transporter of DKC remains unknown. Using transcriptome profiling and a yeast expression system, OsPDR17, an ABCG transporter, was identified and functionally characterized as the major DKC transporter. Its role during Xanthomonas oryzae pv oryzae infection was examined via CRISPR/Cas9 and overexpression, and a transcription factor regulating OsPDR17 was identified. OsPDR17 was localized to the chloroplast membrane, and key enzymes for DKC biosynthesis were chloroplast‐localized proteins. OsPDR17 knockout significantly suppressed the expression of DKC biosynthetic genes, reduced DKC accumulation, and weakened resistance to bacterial blight, whereas overexpression of OsPDR17 showed opposite effects. Notably, we revealed that residue D1149 was essential for OsPDR17‐DKC the interaction using molecular docking and site‐directed mutagenesis analysis. In addition, WRKY10, a known transcription factor of DKC biosynthetic genes, was found to be potentially involved in regulating OsPDR17 expression. Taken together, this work uncovered the pivotal function of OsPDR17 in rice resistance to bacterial blight, mediating the transport of phytoalexin DKC and orchestrating feedback regulation of DKC biosynthesis. These results offered a theoretical insight and an important genetic resource for rice disease resistance research.

articles.title: Beyond ideal cavities: quantifying the impact of cavity dissipation on light-matter strong coupling
articles.abstract: Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics (Cavity-QED) offers a powerful framework for controlling light-matter interactions, yet first-principles approaches commonly assume ideal, lossless cavity fields. Here, we introduce a minimal extension to the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian that accounts for cavity dissipation through the experimentally accessible cavity quality factor Q. The electromagnetic field is described as a damped harmonic oscillator within the very weak damping approximation. In this framework, cavity losses only enter the light-matter interaction and dipole self-energy terms, without introducing additional photonic degrees of freedom. A time-dependent unitary transformation yields a real-valued Hermitian Hamiltonian that can be incorporated into existing ab-initio QED methods without additional computational cost or changes in scaling. We combined the approach to the QED-CCSD method and investigated the effects of cavity dissipation on the optical spectrum of a p-nitroaniline molecule under strong light-matter coupling. We found that, for realistic quality factors, cavity dissipation can reduce the Rabi splitting by more than 20% compared to the ideal-cavity limit, even though the system remains in the strong-coupling regime. Convergence towards the ideal-cavity limit then requires substantially higher quality factors than those needed to establish strong coupling. These results demonstrate that cavity dissipation can significantly affect polaritonic energetics and highlight the importance of incorporating experimentally realistic cavity losses into quantitative ab-initio Cavity-QED simulations to accurately guide experimental protocols.

articles.title: Dielectric Response of Short and Long Range Models of Nonuniform Liquids and Implications for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
articles.abstract: Dielectric screening of electric fields is modified by interfaces and confinement, and any accurate description of interfacial chemistry necessitates properly modeling the nonuniform dielectric tensor. However, models with short range interactions, such as local machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), are increasingly used in simulations of molecular interfaces without quantitative understanding of their nonuniform dielectric response. To build this understanding, we use the framework provided by local molecular field (LMF) theory to quantify the roles of short and long range electrostatics in confined water. Short and long range models predict the same transverse dielectric profile but short range models predict qualitatively different longitudinal dielectric profiles than their long range counterparts. To understand these differences, we develop a Landau theory that shows that long range interactions stiffen polarization fluctuations by a factor of the bulk dielectric constant and reduce the interfacial polarization correlation length by an order of magnitude. LMF theory, which captures long range interactions with an averaged field, can correct the structure and dielectric response, but the standard fluctuation relation no longer holds. We derive a fluctuation relation and integral equation for LMF theory and demonstrate their accuracy for predicting longitudinal dielectric response. MLIPs that incorporate interfacial configurations in their training essentially learn a static mean field correction at the interface, such that the integral equation can be used to predict their nonuniform dielectric profile from polarization fluctuations. We also show that short range MLIPs can be combined with symmetry preserving mean field (SPMF) theory to provide a linear-scaling alternative for long range interactions and predicting nonuniform dielectric functions.

articles.title: Boosting CO2-to-Aviation Fuel Fraction over an Inverse Structured KFeZr Tandem Catalyst
articles.abstract: CO2 hydrogenation to aviation fuel-range hydrocarbons (C8–C16) offers a route to lowering net carbon emissions in the aviation sector, but achieving high selectivity to this fraction remains challenging. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy integrating an inverse-structured KFeZr catalyst with a CO-mediated “hydrogen pump” mechanism over HZSM-5. The inverse architecture, characterized by highly dispersed ZrO2 nanodomains anchored on Fe phases, induces strong metal interactions that stabilize an optimal phase composition (Fe5C2/Fe3O4 ≈ 1.2). This configuration not only provides physical passivation of over-active chain-growth sites but also yields enriched oxygen vacancies and an approximately 3.2-fold increase in interfacial site density compared to conventional counterparts. Upon coupling with HZSM-5, the tandem system delivers a 22% increase in selectivity for the aviation fuel-range fraction. Mechanistic studies identify CO as a “hydrogen pump” that regulates hydrogen transfer within the zeolite, thereby promoting dehydrocyclization and aromatization; introducing CO into the feed further raises this selectivity to 39.7%. This work provides critical insights into interfacial design and intermediate-mediated hydrogen regulation for high-performance liquid fuel synthesis.

articles.title: Carbon-Supported Pt-Rich Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-Pt Nanoparticles for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Reaction
articles.abstract: In this work, a fast moving bed pyrolysis method was used for the synthesis of multimetal catalyst nanoparticles, which have higher ORR activity and durability than those of the Pt–C catalyst synthesized by the same method and a commercial Pt–C catalyst. Carbon-supported multimetal catalyst nanoparticles (Cr10Mn10Fe10Co10Ni10Pt50) were synthesized, and the Pt fraction increased from 55 to 66 at% by acid washing. Structural characterization revealed that multimetal catalysts consist of well-dispersed nanoparticles, whose diffraction patterns were assigned to an L10-type ordered intermetallic structure rather than to the disordered fcc structure characteristic of the conventional CrMnFeCoNi Cantor alloy. The mass and specific activities (MA, SA) of both catalysts in 0.1 M HClO4 at 0.9 V vs RHE are approximately three times higher than those for commercial Pt–C, reaching 780 A gPt–1 and 17 A mPt–2, respectively. The activity enhancement reflects a genuine increase in intrinsic site activity rather than a surface area effect. After 10,000 potential cycles, the multimetal catalysts retained 84–87% of their initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), compared with 66% for commercial Pt–C. Although the multimetal catalysts showed lower relative retention of MA and SA than commercial Pt–C, their higher initial activities resulted in substantially higher absolute ORR activities after cycling. Degradation analysis indicated selective dissolution of 3d metals during potential cycling and possible Pt redeposition, reinforcing the formation of a Pt-rich near-surface region, which contributes to higher retention of the ECSA of these catalysts. This performance arises from the combination of an ordered L10 intermetallic structure, a Pt-rich near-surface region, and a chemically complex subsurface, enabling high intrinsic ORR activity while mitigating the loss of electrochemically accessible Pt surface area.

articles.title: Heterogenization of Ru(bda) Molecular Catalyst with Redox-Active and Proton-Buffering Porphyrin Linkers for Acidic Water Oxidation
articles.abstract: We report a porphyrin-bridged Ru(bda) coordination polymer integrated with carbon nanotubes, constructed from the well-defined homogeneous water oxidation catalyst in acid. The porphyrin linker simultaneously provides redox activity and proton-buffering functionality, enabling acidic water oxidation at an ultralow Ru loading (0.021 mgRu·cm–2). The resulting composite reaches current densities up to 200 mA·cm–2 in acid, exceeding previously reported molecular water oxidation catalyst-based anodes by one to two orders of magnitude. At identical metal loadings, it also outperforms both RuO2 and IrO2 benchmarks in both activity and stability. Electrochemical, spectroscopic, and theoretical results support porphyrin protonation and reversible oxidation, suggesting that ligand redox activity, together with proton management, contributes to the enhanced catalytic performance. These findings underscore the transformative potential of ligand engineering in molecular integration strategies for advancing artificial photosynthetic energy conversion systems.

articles.title: The Chameleon Role of Interfacial Hydroxyls: Reaction-Condition-Dependent Dynamics in Methanol Electro-Oxidation
articles.abstract: The electrocatalytic oxidation of methanol on platinum represents a model system for alcohol fuel-cell chemistry, yet the precise role of interfacial hydroxyl (OH*), a key oxidative species, remains contentious and is often viewed simplistically as either a co-reactant or a poison. Herein, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations with explicit solvation were employed to transcend this binary perspective, revealing OH* as a dynamic interfacial mediator whose coverage influences methanol activation and mechanistic pathways. Under oxidative potentials, increasing OH* coverage leads to the formation of an interfacial adsorbate layer interconnected by hydrogen bonds. Frequent proton transfer within this layer facilitates spontaneous O–H bond cleavage of methanol, while fluctuations in the hydrogen-bond network further promote its pre-oxidation and activation. In contrast, OH*-mediated C–H oxidation involves a high free-energy barrier, and increasing OH* coverage reduces the availability of Pt sites required for C–H dissociation, potentially contributing to surface poisoning. Importantly, site competition induced by high OH* coverage also alters the configuration of the reaction-generated HCHO intermediate, reducing the accessibility of further C–H cleavage toward CO* while enabling direct reaction with OH* toward formate through a CO*-free pathway. Together, these results reveal a coverage-dependent trade-off among O–H activation, the availability of Pt sites for C–H bond cleavage, and subsequent pathway selection. Regulating interfacial OH* coverage therefore provides a possible means to tune methanol oxidation activity and pathway selectivity.

articles.title: A Hybrid Phosphate–Ether Electrolyte for High-Temperature and High-Safety 18650 Cylindrical Sodium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) for grid-scale energy storage require electrolytes with high-temperature durability and intrinsic safety. Here, we report a nonflammable triethyl phosphate/tetrahydrofuran (TEP/THF) hybrid electrolyte for high-temperature SIBs. Weakly coordinating THF increases anion participation in the Na+ solvation structure, promoting robust inorganic-rich interphases on both electrodes, while its low viscosity accelerates Na+ transport, enabling fast ion kinetics and stable interfacial chemistry. As a result, Prussian blue||hard carbon full cells exhibit good rate capability and retain 76.0% capacity after 500 cycles at 80 °C, and 18650 cylindrical cells maintain 80.6% capacity after 300 cycles at 80 °C. Nail-penetration tests show no combustion or smoke, with a peak temperature of only 88.9 °C. Moreover, the electrolyte also supports stable cycling of layered oxide cathodes at 80 °C. This work provides a viable electrolyte design strategy for high-temperature and high-safety SIBs.

articles.title: Modeling Approaches for Polymer-Based Electrolytes in Advanced Batteries: Bridging Processing, Structure, and Performance
articles.abstract: Polymer-based electrolytes are increasingly important in advanced batteries because of their structural tunability, mechanical compliance, and compatibility with diverse electrode and cell architectures. Their behavior depends on transport, interfacial, mechanical, and structural processes that span multiple scales and are shaped by formulation and processing history. This Perspective examines how modeling can be applied to polymer-based electrolyte systems in batteries and introduces a framework based on modeling objective, modeling basis, characteristic scale or data level, and degree of process coupling. Battery-relevant ionogel studies are used to map current modeling emphases and underrepresented directions, while polymer-electrolyte-containing composite electrodes illustrate challenges associated with process-generated microstructure and multifunctional polymer phases. Broader gaps are identified in material-state definition, experiment-model information transfer, structural representation, and process coupling. Progress therefore depends not simply on adding isolated models but on developing transparent, experimentally anchored workflows that establish testable links among formulation, processing, structure, transport, and battery-relevant performance.

articles.title: Understanding the Role of Lithium Metal Microstructure in Chemo-Mechanical Instability of Solid-State Batteries
articles.abstract: Increased energy density and safety relative to conventional lithium (Li)-ion batteries motivate the development of solid-state batteries (SSBs). However, maintaining interface stability at the metal anode–solid electrolyte (SE) interface remains a critical challenge to achieving practical areal capacities, especially during stripping/discharge. Here, a mesoscale model informed by atomistic simulations is employed to examine void formation at the Li metal–SE interface during discharge/stripping. The model reveals how void-formation-driven interfacial contact loss behavior depends on the microstructural properties of the polycrystalline Li anode. In agreement with prior studies, Li microstructures with small grain sizes promote self-diffusion-induced void healing and generally exhibit better interfacial contact. We further show the effect of operating conditions, such as applied pressure, stripping current density, and temperature, on the stripping performance for different Li microstructures. Through this study, we shed light on the importance of taking microstructural features into account in predicting interfacial contact evolution during stripping of Li metal SSBs.

articles.title: Accelerated Electrolyte Engineering by Deep Learning: A Quaternary Ammonium Additive Enables Ultra-Stable Zinc Anodes
articles.abstract: Currently, achieving long-cycling zinc anodes for aqueous zinc-ion energy storage devices remains a challenge owing to uncontrolled dendritic growth and concurrent hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Electrolyte engineering via molecular additives has emerged as an effective strategy for modulating zinc anode interfacial chemistry, but the vast structural space of candidate molecules renders conventional trial-and-error screening inefficient. Here, we present a deep learning (DL) framework for screening high-performance quaternary ammonium cation (QAC) additives for aqueous zinc electrolytes. We developed GATGLP, a graph attention network-based HOMO–LUMO gap (Gap) predictor, to address the data scarcity inherent in ionic molecular systems, which was first pretrained on a curated subset of the QM9 molecular data set and subsequently fine-tuned via transfer learning on a DFT-calculated QAC data set. Through a dual-descriptor screening strategy based on the predicted Gap and the octanol–water partition coefficient (XlogP), a validated library of 378 QAC compounds was ranked, and three candidates were selected for systematic electrochemical validation. Among them, n-octyltrimethylammonium bromide ([N8111]Br) showed a Zn//Zn cycling duration of more than 1800 h at 1 mA cm–2/1 mAh cm–2 and a cycling lifespan of approximately 180 h at 5 mA cm–2/5 mAh cm–2. Across the ZSO-Br, N6111 and N8111 electrolytes, which share the same bromide concentration, three quantities measured by different methods show the same ordering: the relative (002) diffraction proportion, the maximum −Z″ of the impedance arc, and the Zn//Cu sequence length increase from ZSO-Br to N6111 to N8111. The chronoamperometric transient does not follow this ordering, but N8111 is the only electrolyte in which the current magnitude decreases during the step. Taken together, these observations suggest that the selected organic cations may differ in their interfacial accumulation, which could redistribute the Zn deposition flux and contribute to flatter, more continuous deposits. This work combines DL-assisted molecular screening with experimental validation to identify QAC additives for aqueous zinc electrolytes.

articles.title: Reversible Phase-Transition-Enabled Broadband Infrared Photodetection in 1T-TaS2
articles.abstract: Broadband infrared photodetectors operating at room temperature are fundamentally limited by the lack of efficient gain mechanisms for weak optical signals. Phase-transition materials provide a promising route for intrinsic signal amplification owing to their extreme sensitivity near critical transition boundaries. However, the strong thermal hysteresis associated with phase transitions often leads to irreversible switching and poor operational stability, limiting their application in photodetection. Here, we demonstrate a reversible phase-transition-enabled infrared photodetector based on few-layer 1T-TaS2. By integrating the device onto a suspended 200 nm SiNx membrane and employing a pulsed-bias driving scheme, cumulative Joule heating is suppressed while preserving threshold triggered charge-density-wave phase transition, enabling stable and reversible collective conductivity switching. Operating through phase-transition amplification rather than conventional photoconductive or bolometric mechanisms, the device exhibits broadband response from 0.45 to 10.6 μm, with a maximum responsivity of 3.13 × 104 A/W and a detectivity of 3.8 × 1010 Jones, along with fast response times (74 μs rise and 17 μs fall) and excellent cycling stability. Furthermore, reliable blackbody detection is achieved for blackbody source temperatures ranging from 773 to 1373 K, highlighting its potential for uncooled infrared photodetection. These results establish reversible phase-transition amplification as an effective strategy for high-sensitivity photodetection and provide a general framework for optoelectronic sensing based on collective electronic phase transitions.

articles.title: Selective Ultrafast Excitation and Dephasing of Gap Plasmons into Hot Carriers in Structural Color Generation
articles.abstract: Plasmon-induced hot-carriers generated through Landau damping underpin applications in plasmonic optoelectronics, energy conversion, and photocatalysis. However, it remains unclear whether these carriers retain the spatial localization of their parent plasmon modes or rapidly lose this spatial memory through ultrafast scattering and transport. Here, we experimentally probe the spatial and temporal dynamics of plasmon-induced hot-carriers in a strongly confined plasmonic structural color consisting of disordered aluminum nanoparticle ensembles on near-field cavities. Strong interparticle coupling produces hybridized and localized gap plasmon modes with intense nanoscale electromagnetic confinement, which we directly visualize using scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy. Ultrafast pump–probe measurements selectively excite a homogeneously broadened sub-ensemble of plasmonic modes, enabling indirect tracking of pump-generated, plasmon-induced hot-carrier dynamics. We observe that hot-carriers undergo only partial spatial delocalization and retain signatures of the initial plasmonic localization for hundreds of picoseconds. The perturbed sub-ensemble reaches maximum line widths of 0.54 ± 0.06 eV (0.36 ± 0.05 eV) under 630 nm (700 nm) excitation. On a phenomenological localization scale from 0 (localized) to 1 (fully delocalized), this corresponds to 0.35 ± 0.10 and 0.09 ± 0.08 for 630 and 700 nm excitation, respectively. The wavelength-dependent fraction shows that the degree of preserved localization is optically tunable, set by the carrier energy. This persistence of spatial memory, likely arising from disorder-induced scattering within the nanoparticle ensemble, reveals an unexpected spatial dimension of hot-carrier dynamics and highlights the role of plasmonic confinement and structural disorder in governing nanoscale energy flow, with implications for hot-carrier-based optoelectronics.

articles.title: Spin-State Engineering for Multi-Electron Reactions: Active Sites and Reaction Mechanisms
articles.abstract: Multi-electron-proton coupling reactions are fundamental in renewable energy conversion and environmental cleanup. However, achieving high catalytic efficiency and product selectivity remains a formidable challenge, primarily due to the complex transformations of intermediates, sluggish reaction kinetics, and intense competition from side reactions. In recent years, spin regulation has emerged as a crucial strategy to address these issues. By engineering spin states and controlling spin polarization, the electronic structure of catalysts can be effectively reconfigured, thereby optimizing the adsorption and desorption of intermediates and regulating charge transport and reaction pathways. This review comprehensively summarizes recent progress in spin-regulation strategies for key multi-electron reactions, including CO2RR, NRR/NO3RR, ORR, and water-splitting catalysis involving OER and HER, and further examines the roles of structural identity and reaction-dependent spin-electronic configurations in governing active-site function. We emphasize that different local spin configurations can each enhance catalytic performance under appropriate reaction conditions, whereas no single spin state can be regarded as universally superior. Accordingly, identification of the operative active site requires consideration of both its structural identity and its reaction-dependent spin-electronic state under working conditions. Within this framework, special attention is given to the roles of doping, defect engineering, coordination modulation, external fields, and multimetallic cooperation in regulating active-site identity, intermediate energetics, charge transfer, and product selectivity. Finally, we discuss current challenges and future directions for identifying operative active sites and establishing predictive design principles for efficient multi-electron catalysis. Overall, this review provides mechanistic insights and practical guidance for identifying operative spin-regulated active sites and rationally designing efficient and selective catalysts for multi-electron reactions.

articles.title: Two-terminal photoelectric synapses for attojoule neuromorphic vision
articles.abstract: Two-terminal photoelectric synapses integrate sensing, memory, and computation for neuromorphic vision. This review connects materials, mechanisms, and system design toward attojoule-scale, scalable, and sustainable neuromorphic hardware.

articles.title: Accelerating Identification of Relevant Polarons in Batteries
articles.abstract: Many of the materials under consideration as battery electrodes are known to exhibit polarons─charge carriers localized through polarizing their environments, which are unfortunately quite costly to tackle by theory. Next to costly ab initio methods and geometry optimizations, the main problem is the sheer number of possible configurations polarons can adopt in a material. This problem is exacerbated by symmetry-breaking defects such as oxygen vacancies ubiquitous in oxide materials. Fortunately, a majority of polaron configurations tend to be too high in energy to ever be adopted at normal operating temperatures. In this work, we therefore present a data-driven approach based on gradient-boosted decision trees as a descriptor for relative polaron energies. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach to weed out those configurations that are energetically unlikely in three simulation cells of defected spinel Lithium4Titanium5Oxygen12 (LTO). The first two cells differ by their 16d-site occupational disorder and the position of the oxygen vacancy, which in both cases leads to the formation of two polarons in the cells. In contrast, the third simulation cell contains an extra lithium ion, which leads to three polarons. Our approach allows us to reduce the number of necessary first-principles calculations by roughly two-thirds. It can easily be adapted to other materials and simulation cells, greatly speeding up their theoretical treatment.

articles.title: Lithium Makes the Difference─Evolution of Lithium Vacancy Disorder during Temperature-Induced Phase Transitions of the Li-Ion Conductor Li4SnS4
articles.abstract: Sulfide-based lithium-ion solid electrolytes are promising candidates for solid-state batteries due to their high ionic conductivities, although they typically exhibit high moisture sensitivity. Li4SnS4 has recently attracted scientific interest because it exhibits higher moisture resistance than most other sulfide electrolytes. Two orthorhombic Li4SnS4 polymorphs (α and β) are known, yet their temperature-dependent phase behavior remains unexplored. Differential scanning calorimetry and temperature-dependent powder X-ray diffraction revealed that α-Li4SnS4 transitions to β-Li4SnS4 at 96 °C. Furthermore, we identified a second, previously unknown reversible phase transition from β-Li4SnS4 to a new γ-polymorph at 196 °C. Other phase transitions from −150°C to 1000°C were not identified. All polymorphs crystallize in space group Pnma (no. 62) and feature identical zig-zag-like arrangements of SnS44– tetrahedra. The main structural differences lie in the ordering of the lithium substructure. By combining temperature-dependent powder X-ray and neutron diffraction with high-temperature 7Li and 119Sn NMR as well as Raman spectroscopy, we show that Li4SnS4 transitions from the lithium-vacancy-disordered α-phase to the ordered β-phase and finally to the disordered γ-Li4SnS4. Using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we measured ionic conductivities from 10–6 S cm–1 to 10–1 S cm–1 between 25 °C to 220 °C. Conductivity changes are gradual, consistent with the subtle structural variations among all polymorphs.

articles.title: Nucleation and Coalescence of Wüstite-like Motifs in Oxygen-Deficient Magnetite: A Deep-Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
articles.abstract: Oxygen loss in magnetite drives the cation redistribution and local structural reconstruction that control the rate of iron oxide reduction, but this coupling has resisted direct simulation: the reconstruction develops far beyond DFT-accessible scales, and classical potentials cannot describe mixed-valence Fe–O with the required fidelity. We developed a DFT-validated Fe–O Deep Potential trained on bulk, defective, and surface configurations and applied it in large-scale molecular dynamics with an imposed stochastic oxygen-removal protocol. The potential reproduces DFT energy and force trends together with vacancy and surface energetics. DFT single-point checks on oxygen-deficient configurations and equation-of-state calculations for Fe3O4 and FeO further delineate the transferability of the potential, with larger deviations emerging in the most strongly oxygen-deficient states. As oxygen is removed, four-coordinated O environments decrease while six-coordinated wüstite-like motifs emerge, grow, and coalesce into extended local domains. Deep-Potential nudged elastic band (DP-NEB) calculations, benchmarked against selected DFT single-point energies, show that the coupled O/Fe-vacancy configuration gives the lowest Fe-migration barrier among the selected local rearrangement pathways. Time-windowed mean-squared displacements yield apparent Fe and O diffusivities that evolve in the nonstationary lattice. These simulations establish a defect-mediated solid-state response toward wüstite-like local order under imposed oxygen-deficient conditions, rather than the formation of a complete equilibrium Fe1–xO phase. The protocol isolates oxide-side reconstruction and does not explicitly treat hydrogen chemistry.

articles.title: A Genetic Method for Distinguishing Cryptic Pocillopora Species in French Polynesia Without Sequencing
articles.abstract: Pocillopora is a widespread, dominant reef‐building coral genus in the Indo‐Pacific; many species within this group exhibit high morphological similarity and plasticity. Given this, genetic tools are needed to robustly identify Pocillopora individuals to the species level. Quick and accurate identification approaches for Pocillopora species are critical to estimating biodiversity patterns under current and future environmental challenges. In recent years, the mitochondrial open reading frame (mtORF) and a histone region (PocHistone) have been validated using genome‐wide data to become the most widely used species‐level markers for Pocillopora. However, Sanger sequencing of a large number of samples can be prohibitively expensive and sequencing facilities are not always readily available. Therefore, we present restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) digests here that identify the six species of Pocillopora (P. acuta, P. cf. effusa, P. grandis, P. meandrina, P. tuahiniensis, and P. verrucosa) found in French Polynesia, without sequencing. In uninformed validation tests (in silico and in vitro), our protocol identified each Pocillopora species with 100% accuracy. Given their cost‐effective, rapid nature, the tailoring of additional RFLP digest protocols to identify cryptic coral species in reef regions around the world will support foundational reef science, conservation and restoration initiatives.

articles.title: Functional Profiles of Fish Gut Microbiota Associated With Feeding Habits in the Midstream of the Jialing River Under Cascade Channelization
articles.abstract: To examine the influence of diet on fish gut microbiota in channelized rivers, we characterized the gut microbial communities of fish with different feeding habits in the midstream of the Jialing River. The main findings are as follows: (1) 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing identified Firmicutes and Proteobacteria as the dominant phyla, with their relative abundances differing significantly among fish of distinct feeding habits. Firmicutes exhibited the highest relative abundance in carnivorous fish (93.41%), followed by omnivorous (53.39%) and herbivorous fish (29.3%). In contrast, Proteobacteria was most abundant in herbivorous fish (32.72%), with lower levels in omnivorous (22.43%) and carnivorous fish (4.81%). (2) The Kruskal–Wallis test indicated significant differences in the α-diversity of gut microbial communities among fish with distinct feeding habits (p < 0.05), where herbivorous fish presented the highest α-diversity, followed by omnivorous fish, with carnivorous fish exhibiting the lowest. PERMANOVA analysis showed that the feeding habits significantly influenced gut microbial community structure (Pseudo-F = 3.85, R 2 = 0.18033, p < 0.05). (3) PICRUSt2 functional prediction analysis showed that omnivorous fish in the midstream of the Jialing River had a higher relative abundance of pathways related to microbial metabolism in diverse environments (4.792% ± 0.221%). In comparison, herbivorous fish had a higher relative abundance of pathways related to carbon fixation pathways in prokaryotes (0.927% ± 0.091%). In contrast, carnivorous fish not only had a higher relative abundance of the cysteine and methionine metabolism pathway (1.026% ± 0.051%) but also showed higher relative abundances of pathways related to carbohydrate utilization, including starch and sucrose metabolism (0.768% ± 0.031%) and the phosphotransferase system (PTS) (0.461% ± 0.019%), which may be associated with habitat homogenization following channelization. These findings provide a reference for habitat restoration in channelized rivers and the conservation of fish resources.

articles.title: Patterns in Coral Fecundity Across the Indo‐Pacific
articles.abstract: Coral reproductive potential is a fundamental component of reef resistance and recovery, yet large‐scale estimates of reproductive potential remain limited. This study generated the first large‐scale approximation of coral reproductive potential across the Indo‐Pacific by integrating coral fecundity, trait‐based imputation, and coral cover data. Reproductive potential was estimated for 277 coral species from 55 genera, including key genera such as Acropora, Isopora, Montipora, and Porites, for a single, hypothetical spawning period. We combined empirical coral fecundity datasets with trait‐based imputation approaches to estimate reproductive potential at three levels: fecundity per cm2, colony fecundity, and total fecundity across the Indo‐Pacific. These fecundity estimates were then integrated with regional coral cover to derive a first‐order approximation of reproductive potential. The estimated total reproductive potential of Indo‐Pacific corals was approximately three quintillion eggs (3.46 × 1018) for one hypothetical spawning period. Fecundity varied significantly across genera and growth forms, with Isopora, Acropora, and Montipora contributing disproportionately to total egg production (mean totals of 3.9 × 1016, 4.2 × 1015, and 3.49 × 1015 eggs, respectively). Branching and massive growth forms collectively accounted for roughly 50% of total fecundity across all levels. Species‐level fecundity was not consistently aligned with genus‐level trends, with some species exhibiting exceptionally high fecundity at the species level despite relatively low average fecundity at the level of genus. Concordance across the three fecundity levels was low, highlighting substantial variation within genera and potential gaps in our current understanding of coral reproductive potential, likely both. This study provides the first quantitative approximation of Indo‐Pacific coral reproductive potential, demonstrating high variation across species, genera, and growth forms. These findings underscore the importance of multi‐scale reproductive assessments and offer a data‐driven foundation for identifying key taxa for conservation or restoration efforts based on their disproportionately high contribution to reef recovery.

articles.title: Phylogenomics Clarifies Plastome Reduction and Phylogenetic Relationships in Monotropoideae
articles.abstract: Plastome evolution and biogeographic history remain poorly understood in mycoheterotrophic lineages. Here, we sequenced and assembled the complete plastome of Monotropa callistoma (Ericaceae), a fully mycoheterotrophic species, and compared it with other mycoheterotrophic plastomes. The M. callistoma plastome is 29,784 bp long, lacks the canonical quadripartite structure, and contains 40 genes, representing an intermediate level of reduction within Monotropoideae. Comparative analyses revealed extreme contraction in some lineages, including Sciaphila (12.8–21.5 kb), and a weak positive correlation between GC content and genome size. Within Monotropoideae, plastomes become smaller from the early‐branching Pterospora lineage to the more recently diverged Monotropa lineage. This reduction is accompanied by progressively poorer synteny and lineage‐specific loss of rps23 in Monotropa. Phylogenomic analyses of 30 Ericaceae plastomes strongly supported Monotropoideae (bootstrap = 100) and clarified relationships among its 10 sampled genera. Divergence‐time estimation and ancestral‐range reconstruction placed the origin of Clade 1 (Pyroloideae, Arbutoideae and Monotropoideae) in Asia during the late Cretaceous to early Cenozoic. The lineage subsequently dispersed to North America via Beringia, whereas the Monotropsis + Monotropastrum + Monotropa clade later dispersed back to Asia during the late Eocene to early Oligocene. This history gave rise to East Asian endemics, including Monotropa humile and M. callistoma. These findings illuminate plastome reduction in mycoheterotrophs, resolve relationships within Monotropoideae, and support a complex history of bidirectional intercontinental dispersal.

Paleoecological dynamics of the Jurassic-Cretaceous transition: insights from the Vaca Muerta Formation marine biota
articles.abstract: The global understanding of the functioning of Mesozoic marine ecosystems has historically been heavily biased toward paleoecological models based on Northern Hemisphere localities with exceptional preservation; meanwhile, highly fossiliferous Western Gondwana sites remained poorly addressed. To contribute to filling this gap, this study provides the first integrated, multi-trophic paleoecological reconstruction of both marine macroinvertebrate and vertebrate associations in Western Gondwana. We synthesize and analyze two age- and stratigraphically constrained taxonomic datasets from different paleogeographic positions over the carbonate ramp of the Vaca Muerta Formation (Neuquén Basin, Argentina): the Sierra de la Cara Cura and Cerro Lotena sections. The data obtained enabled us to evaluate ecosystem dynamics using quantitative and qualitative tools, including Westermann Morphospace modeling, multi-level benthic tiering, and vertebrate trophic-guild analyses. The results reveal a complex, vertically stratified pelagic realm that remained functionally stable for over nine million years. The vertebrate assemblage is abundant and taxonomically diverse, including top predators and more specialized forms. Actinopterygian fishes, particularly, displayed a wide range of body shapes, locomotor modes, and feeding strategies, spanning pelagic to demersal/benthic habitats and encompassing suspension-feeding, invertivorous, microphagous, piscivorous, and durophagous forms. Mesopredatory marine reptiles’ morphological disparity suggests strict niche partitioning despite preying upon similar food sources. Ammonite communities tracked a shallowing-upward trend, shifting from early Tithonian streamlined, demersal active swimmers into heavily sculptured planktonic drifters mechanically adapted to storm-dominated environments. Conversely, the benthic realm dynamics remained decoupled from the water column and were strictly regulated by oxygenation, water energy, and substrate consistency variations. Benthic invertebrate ecosystems shifted from highly impoverished, opportunistic, or pseudoplanktic communities during the early Tithonian into highly diversified, multi-tiered assemblages punctuated by extensive oyster biostromes as oxygenation improved by the late Berriasian, before a final shallowing trend led to a major ecological reorganization at the Intravalanginian Discontinuity. Direct and indirect evidence on biotic interactions reveal a highly interconnected, complex trophic network, spanning microplanktonic producers to hypercarnivorous reptile apex predators. Ultimately, these findings highlight the coordinated eco-spatial and trophic mechanisms of Gondwanan ecosystems and establish the Neuquén Basin as a critical window into global marine dynamics during the Jurassic–Cretaceous transition.

articles.title: Beyond observed diversity: Community completeness negatively affects ecosystem invasibility across scales
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Charles Elton proposed that species‐rich communities are more resistant to invasion, yet a well‐known paradox persists: native diversity suppresses invasion at small scales while correlating positively with non‐native species diversity at broad scales. Moving beyond native observed diversity alone to community completeness, defined as the ratio of native observed diversity to its specific species pool, may offer a potential framework to address this scale dependency. This is because the completeness index reflects the degree to which a habitat saturates its available niche space, shaped jointly by abiotic and biotic filtering in an origin‐blind manner. At small spatial scales, native observed diversity and dark diversity (suitable yet absent native species) are negatively correlated. This implies that high native observed diversity indicates high community completeness, leaving limited vacant niche opportunities for both un‐arrived native and non‐native species and thus reducing invasibility. In contrast, at large spatial scales, greater environmental heterogeneity can yield a vastly expanded regional species pool where dark diversity also accumulates more, potentially resulting in lower community completeness and heightened susceptibility. It should be noted that native community completeness, based on the extant species pool, fails to capture the niche spaces left by historical species losses—a gap tracked by temporal dark diversity dynamics—yet these hypervolume holes can instead be successfully exploited and predicted by non‐native community completeness. Following on this logic, I propose a Completeness‐Based Invasion Theory, which hypothesizes that community invasibility is inversely related to community completeness across spatial scales. While further empirical testing across diverse systems is required, measuring completeness alongside observed diversity may provide a novel, scale‐independent perspective to advance our understanding and management of biological invasions. Combining both native community completeness and non‐native community completeness to predict non‐native species invasions may currently represent the optimal approach. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Plant‐derived compounds to improve soil inoculation for restoration
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Restoring the soil microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important requirement for the success of ecosystem restoration. Soil inoculation can reintroduce the missing taxa, but its application is limited by the large amount of donor soil that is needed and by the poor persistence of the inoculants, because of habitat filtering, priority effects and the loss of plant–microbe feedbacks. Here we propose the metabolite‐inoculum approach, a framework that combines the chemical diversity of plants with soil inoculation, in order to improve the establishment, persistence and effectiveness of introduced microbial communities. In this framework, the chemical input is delivered as fresh and dead plant material, as extracts of this material or as purified compounds that are applied together with the inoculum, and not by adding or manipulating the living plant community. We first synthesize the evidence that plant metabolites, from both above‐ and below‐ground tissues, act as selective regulators of soil microbial composition and diversity. Building on this, we propose a framework for the selection of plant materials and metabolites at the species, tissue and compound levels, and we introduce the parallel concepts of core and keystone metabolites that are matched to their corresponding microbial groups. We then identify the main challenges of the approach, the mismatch in timescale, the non‐target effects and the feasibility, and we translate them into testable hypotheses. Finally, we discuss the contexts in which the approach is likely to work and the contexts in which it is not. In this way, we frame the metabolite‐inoculum approach as a research agenda through bridging chemical ecology and microbial ecology, offering a potential solution to reduce dependency on donor soil, improve inoculant effectiveness and accelerate the recovery of degraded soils toward desired ecosystem states. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Tree species identity is associated with rhizosphere microbiome assembly via root metabolite‐mediated feedbacks in subtropical forests
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The rhizosphere microbiome is critical for forest ecological functions, yet the mechanisms through which tree species identity and neighbour tree interactions are associated with its assembly remain poorly understood. Using Illumina MiSeq and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), we investigated how tree species (pine vs. liquidambar) and forest composition (pure vs. mixed) shape rhizosphere microbial communities and root metabolites in subtropical forests. Rhizosphere fungal community structure differed significantly across rhizosphere types, whereas bacterial community and metabolite profiles differed primarily between the pure pine forest and other forest types. Predicted functional shifts included a decline in cellulolytic bacteria (−27%) and an increase in denitrifying groups (+54%), with ectomycorrhizal fungi enriched in mixed than pure forests (p < 0.05). Metabolite profiling revealed that lipids, organic acids and sugars were the most abundant compound classes, with 55 metabolites differentially abundant between pure pine and mixed forest rhizospheres. Rhizosphere metabolite profiles were significantly correlated with microbial community structure (p < 0.05). Specific microbe–metabolite associations were identified; fatty acids positively correlated with oligotrophic bacteria (WPS‐2), sugars with denitrifiers (Reyranella) and dipeptides with the beneficial fungus Penicillium. These results demonstrate that tree species identity is associated with rhizosphere microbiome assembly via root metabolite‐associated feedbacks, which correlate with soil nutrient cycling. This provides a mechanistic, function‐oriented framework for understanding plant–microbiome interaction and harnessing them to enhance ecosystem resilience. articles.title: Mosaic Accumulation of Somatic Genetic Variation and Estimates of Age in the Long‐Lived Reef‐Building Coral Acropora palmata
articles.abstract: Somatic genetic variation (SoGV) accumulates during an organism's lifetime and is traditionally viewed as detrimental rather than adaptive due to links with cancer and senescence. However, in modular organisms like corals, deleterious mutations can be purged at the cellular or polyp level, while adaptive mutations may rise in frequency as polyps create genetically distinct modules. Quantifying the somatic genetic landscape in corals is necessary to understand the role these mutations may have in coral and clonal animal development and evolution. Here, we catalogue somatic genetic variation in eight Acropora palmata colonies from Curaçao. Whole genomes were sequenced (70–100× depth) to document mutation variant allele frequency shifts as genets age. Large numbers of SoGVs were observed in six‐ to ten‐year‐old colonies, and inferred mutation rates were used to age a genet of uncertain age to almost a century old. Mutations were not fixed at the polyp or branch levels, i.e., they always displayed frequencies < 0.5 as expected at mutating homozygous sites. However, their allele frequencies followed a power‐law distribution, similar to aging human tissues. No signs of positive selection were found; instead SoGVs were under purifying selection. In one colony, mutations in 28 samples from along a branch were analysed using a SNP microarray. Contrary to expectations, genetic and physical distances were unrelated. Along with an observed lack of fixation this pattern may be explained by a large stem cell population, the de‐differentiation or dormancy of stem cells, the contribution of strong purifying selection, or a combination of the previously mentioned. Our findings provide a neutral framework against which to test for module‐level selection of genetic variation in corals, explore the relationship between physical and genetic distance within a colony, and apply a somatic genetic clock to colonies of Acropora palmata. This work provides fundamental insights into the landscape of somatic mutations in reef‐building coral, highlighting the importance of studying somatic genetic variation as they may contribute to genetic diversity and adaptability in colonial animals.

articles.title: Natural Variation in Drosophila melanogaster Clock PolyQ Length: Geographic Gradients and Functional Properties
articles.abstract: Natural variation in circadian clock genes provides a powerful framework for understanding how organisms respond to environmental heterogeneity. The Clock (Clk) gene encodes a core transcriptional regulator of circadian rhythms and contains a polymorphic polyglutamine (polyQ) tract whose evolutionary significance remains unclear. Here, we integrate population genomic, behavioural, and molecular analyses to investigate the functional and geographic patterns of Clk polyQ variation in Drosophila melanogaster. Using data from 127 European populations, we identify 11 Clk polyQ alleles and find that their frequencies are geographically structured, most consistently along an east–west gradient: the Q25 and Q27 alleles show robust clines in longitude and in a bioclimatic axis of continentality, whereas latitudinal and altitudinal trends are weaker. Behavioural assays of near‐isogenic lines revealed that polyQ length modulates circadian function under thermal challenge: most alleles maintained stable free‐running periods across temperatures, whereas the intermediate‐length Q25 allele showed the strongest, though modest, temperature sensitivity. Circadian phase showed pronounced allele‐specific sensitivity to elevated temperature in laboratory assays, although phase variation did not display a consistent relationship with geographic variables. At the molecular level, luciferase reporter assays showed that longer polyQ alleles exhibited higher transcriptional activity, linking polyQ length to CLK‐mediated gene expression. Together, these results demonstrate that natural variation in Clk polyQ length has measurable functional consequences for circadian regulation and is geographically structured in patterns consistent with underlying climatic variation, highlighting the potential for low‐complexity regions to modulate clock function in a context‐dependent manner across environmental gradients.

articles.title: Defect engineering enables humidity-tolerant crystallization for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells
Ultrahigh performance implantable sono-piezoelectric nanogenerators based on core@dendritic shell ferroelectric nanocomposites for battery-free and wireless-powered bioelectronics
Disordered Near-Field Metasurfaces for On-Chip Wavelength Demultiplexing
articles.abstract: Plasmonic and dielectric building blocks shape the flow of light at boundaries and interfaces. While metasurfaces that consist of plasmonic or dielectric nanophotonic elements have established a framework for shaping the far field, control over near fields remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce disordered metasurfaces for near-field light shaping. Near-field distributions are created by engineering the interference of surface plasmons launched from scatterers on metallic surfaces. We demonstrate near-field metasurfaces to direct, focus, and demultiplex light. These structures use a strip-off process, resulting in ultrasmooth metallic surfaces suitable for efficient surface plasmon propagation. An optical imaging setup enables retrieval of the local near-field by mapping it into the far-field. Our concept can be generalized to arbitrary near-field distributions, permitting nanoscale routing and sorting of light based on polarization and orbital angular momentum, as well as coupling schemes to emitters and nanoscale systems in ultracompact integrated photonic receivers and demultiplexers.

articles.title: Manipulating Crystallization and Deprotonation Reaction through Surface Engineering of ZnO for Bright and Stable Near-Infrared Perovskite LEDs
articles.abstract: Perovskite light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have attracted significant attention owing to their rapidly increasing external quantum efficiencies (EQEs). However, achieving bright and operationally stable perovskite LEDs remains a great challenge. Here, we reveal that the most commonly used surface modifier of zinc-oxide (ZnO) electron-transport layer, polyethylenimine ethoxylate (PEIE), inhibits the perovskite nucleation by inducing in situ chemical reactions of perovskite precursor components, forming thermally unstable interfacial species and reducing long-term operational stability of resultant devices. We develop a surface-engineering strategy by using an ether-based polymer modifier to regulate perovskite crystallization kinetics and simultaneously suppress ZnO-induced deprotonation during long-term device operation. As a result, the optimized near-infrared (NIR) perovskite LEDs exhibit a maximum EQE of 24% and a peak radiance of 539 W sr–1 m–2, along with significantly enhanced operational stability. Furthermore, partial substitution of FA with Cs confirms the generality of this strategy, yielding bright NIR devices with an operational half-lifetime of 561 h at 20 mA cm–2.

articles.title: A crystalline uranium Fischer-type carbyne
articles.abstract: Since their discovery in 1973, transition metal Fischer carbynes have become a foundational class of metal–carbon triple bond in organometallic chemistry. However, even though the uranium Fischer carbyne bonding motif has been a fundamental target in f -element chemistry, its isolation has remained challenging. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of the uranium Fischer-type carbyne complex [N″ 3 U(μ-CNN)UN″ 3 ] (N″ = N(SiMe 3 ) 2 ). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals a uranium–carbyne distance of 2.379(15) Å, and density functional theory calculations combined with experimental quantum crystallography Hirshfeld atom refinement reveal the presence of two-electron C→U σ -donation, weak two-electron C→U π -donations and two orthogonal one-electron U→C π -back-bonds, demonstrating σ 2 π 1 π 1 Fischer-type carbyne bonding overall. This work redefines the range of bonding modes for the diazomethanediide ligand and reveals a uranium–carbon triple-bond interaction that is related, yet distinct from transition metal Fischer carbynes, providing a basis to develop and understand f -element carbyne chemistry.

articles.title: Photoelectrochemical C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling using native functional groups
articles.abstract: Radical–radical cross-coupling provides an efficient route to forming C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds; however, such methods are diffusion controlled and require sensitive catalysts. Now a photoelectrochemical method for constructing C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds directly from native functional groups is reported. Integrating light, electricity and dual-metal catalysis, the process enables selective radical generation and efficient cross-coupling under mild conditions.

articles.title: BpSRK1‐mediated phosphorylation of BpERF3 relieves HDA6‐dependent chromatin repression to enhance drought tolerance in birch
articles.abstract: The TF BpERF3 positively regulates drought tolerance and activates POD‐associated stress‐response genes in birch. Summary Drought tolerance in plants requires rapid conversion of water‐deficit signals into protective transcriptional and epigenetic programs. Although ERF transcription factors (TFs) are central regulators of stress‐responsive gene expression, how drought‐induced kinase signaling is coupled to chromatin regulation and antioxidant gene activation remains unclear. Here, we identify the ERF TF BpERF3 as a phosphorylation‐dependent regulator of drought tolerance in birch (Betula platyphylla). Using transgenic and CRISPR‐Cas9 mutant lines, protein interaction assays, immunoaffinity fluorescent electrophoresis (IAFE)‐based interactome mapping, post‐translational modification analysis, reactive oxygen species measurements, and drought phenotyping, we dissected the regulatory mechanism underlying BpERF3‐mediated stress adaptation. We show that BpERF3 activates the peroxidase (POD) genes BpPOD3 and BpPOD4, which are required for its drought‐protective function. Mechanistically, BpSRK1 phosphorylates BpERF3 at Ser355, enabling phosphorylated BpERF3 to competitively engage the HDAC domain of BpHDA6 and restrict BpHDA6‐dependent histone H3.1 deacetylation. Consequently, H3.1 acetylation is maintained, chromatin relaxes, downstream stress‐responsive genes are activated, and drought tolerance is enhanced in birch. Our findings reveal a BpSRK1‐BpERF3‐BpHDA6‐H3.1 regulatory module that links drought‐induced phosphorylation to local chromatin activation and redox homeostasis, providing mechanistic insight into plant stress adaptation.

articles.title: Migratory dermal γδ T cells determine the balance between lung immunity and tissue damage during helminth infection
articles.abstract: Many helminth parasites migrate through multiple host organs during infection, but how immune responses are relayed across these tissues is still poorly understood. To investigate the immune aspects of intertissue communication during infection, we established a percutaneous infection model with the tissue-migrating nematode Nippostrongylus brasiliensis . Profiling of the initial cutaneous immune response revealed that dermal γδ T cells become activated via an interleukin 1 receptor (IL-1R)–dependent mechanism, engage cell motility–associated transcriptional pathways, and leave the skin after parasite invasion. Inhibition of leukocyte migration prevents the accumulation of IL-17–producing γδ T cells in the lungs. Bypassing the skin phase of infection, and thereby preventing dermal γδ T cell migration, dampens early IL-17 production in the lungs. This, instead, leads to an enhanced interferon-γ (IFN-γ) response together with increased lung damage. Collectively, our data highlight a critical skin-lung axis regulating host-parasite interactions and safeguarding lung health.

articles.title: Multiomic analysis of malignant ascites defines RORC-expressing dendritic cells at sites of metastasis
articles.abstract: Malignant ascites is caused by the peritoneal dissemination of cancer and has a poor prognosis. Here, we performed multiomic analyses on ascites samples from patients with cancer and identified RORC -expressing dendritic cells ( RORC DCs) enriched in malignant ascites. RORC DCs expressed PIGR and were transcriptionally similar to murine RORγt + DCs/Thetis cells implicated in immune tolerance. We devised a high-purity sorting strategy to enable in vitro experiments with patient-derived RORC DCs, which indicated that these cells were phenotypically stable and stimulated T cell proliferation while attenuating IFNG expression. Multiplexed immunofluorescence identified RORC DCs in primary tumors and demonstrated their enrichment in regional lymph node metastases. These results associate human RORC DCs with advanced malignancies and suggest a role for these cells in the tumor microenvironment.
